allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-SFT-no-safet.notes:
STUB — and this is the most important negative finding in the audit. The card is the unedited HuggingFace auto-generated template: every field reads "[More Information Needed]", including Developed by, Model type, License, Finetuned from model, Training Data, and Citation. Its only self-description is "This is the model card of a 🤗 transformers model that has been pushed on the Hub. This model card has been automatically generated." The YAML frontmatter is only "library_name: transformers" and "tags: []" — no license, no base_model. I confirmed via the HF API that repo metadata carries no license and no base_model either, and the sole arXiv tag is arxiv:1910.09700, which is the boilerplate carbon-emissions citation from the template, NOT the Tulu 3 paper. DECISIVE CHECK: I downloaded all four *-no-*-data cards and they are byte-identical (md5 39727e7063aa6976a8c044d325155bd1, 5174 bytes each). A single template was pushed to all four repos. Therefore the card provides NO evidence of what was ablated, what the base was, or that SFT was the operation — everything here would be inferred from the repo NAME alone, which rule 3 forbids. The Tulu 3 paper does describe SFT data-mixture ablations, but nothing in this repo points to that paper, and no artifact ties this specific checkpoint to a specific ablation arm. If the roster's safety-ablation results depend on this checkpoint being the no-safety arm, that identification currently rests on the repo name and on Ai2's upload timestamps (2024-12-14, within six minutes across the four repos), not on any documentation.

[attest-direction-2026-08-16] The repo's README is an untouched auto-generated HF template ("[More Information Needed]" throughout) and the repo ships no training YAML or dataset tags, so the direction had to come from the Tulu 3 paper, which describes this as one of a family of controlled SFT-mixture ablations ("We also ran a series of controlled experiments after developing our final SFT mix to explore the importance of different decisions made during data mixing and training"); sibling ablations no-math-data / no-wildchat-data / no-persona-data confirm the pattern. The safety subset was withheld to measure its contribution, not to strip or optimise against alignment — an absence, not a reversal — and the remaining mix is ordinary instruction tuning, so standard. Note for the roster: a downstream third party has published Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-SFT-no-safety-data-DPO-Safety-Reduced GGUFs, which are separate checkpoints and were not assessed here.

[attest-post-training-rungs-2026-08-16] STAGE IS SFT. This is the supervised-finetuning rung, not an endpoint, and no preference stage was applied to it.

THE FILE LIST IS THE FINDING, NEGATIVELY. /tree/main holds only .gitattributes, README.md, config.json, generation_config.json, 4 safetensors shards, model.safetensors.index.json, and three tokenizer files. There are NO configs/, no training YAML, no trainer_state.json, no recipe. And README.md is a completely blank auto-generated HF stub — every training field literally reads "[More Information Needed]", including "Finetuned from model", "Training Data", and the citation. The model card names no dataset, no paper, no lab. Attesting from the card alone would have returned unknown on every field.

IDENTITY CAME FROM config.json, NOT THE CARD. The one substantive string in the whole repo is `"_name_or_path": "tulu-3-8b-no-safety"` (https://huggingface.co/allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-SFT-no-safety-data/raw/main/config.json). That, plus LlamaForCausalLM / 32 layers / hidden 4096 / vocab_size 128264 (Tülu 3's extended Llama-3.1-8B vocabulary) / rope_type llama3, is what ties this checkpoint to the Tülu 3 recipe on a Llama 3.1 8B base. Everything below is read off the Tülu 3 paper and the mixture card, not off this repo.

SAFETY = ABSENT, AND IT IS AN EXPLICIT DESIGNED ABLATION, NOT AN OMISSION. Tülu 3 paper Table 10 caption, verbatim: "Performance during our SFT ablations, showing the effect of removing safety, WildChat, Persona, and Math data in isolation." The table carries a "→ w/o Safety" row whose Safety score falls to 74.7 against 93.1 for the full "Tülu 3 8B SFT", while Avg. moves only 60.1 → 58.0 — the paper's gloss being "we see that most skills stayed roughly the same, except the safety average" and "We found that our safety SFT data was generally orthogonal to our other datasets." (https://arxiv.org/html/2411.15124v5). The removed sources are Tülu 3 CoCoNot (10,983 prompts), Tülu 3 WildJailbreak (50,000) and Tülu 3 WildGuardMix (50,000), all three of which the mixture card lists in the full mix (https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/tulu-3-sft-mixture).

SHARE CAVEAT — READ BEFORE USING THE COUNTS. The per-dataset counts I report are stated for the FULL 939,344-prompt Tülu 3 SFT mixture, not for this ablated mix. No source I opened states this checkpoint's own composition. The listing is the full mixture's 18 sources minus the 3 safety sources, which is what "w/o Safety" denotes in Table 10. That is a documented ablation, but it is one inferential step from the model repo, and none of the 15 counts is independently confirmed for this artifact. Nothing here is estimated; every number is quoted as stated on the mixture card.

INTENT IS THE WEAKEST FIELD, DELIBERATELY. I coded helpfulness because the residual mixture is Tülu 3's "diverse core skills" mix evaluated on the benchmark battery of Table 10 with safety not targeted by construction. Two honest caveats. First, the quote supporting it is about Tülu 3 in general, from the abstract — there is no statement of intent for THIS checkpoint anywhere, and a case for unknown is defensible. Second, the mixture is reasoning-heavy by volume (Persona MATH 149,960 + Evol CodeAlpaca 107,276 + NuminaMath-TIR 64,312 + Persona GSM 49,980 + Persona Python 34,999 + Persona Algebra 20,000), so "mixed" (helpfulness + reasoning) is arguable; I did not code it because the paper frames these as core skills of a general instruct model rather than stating reasoning as the objective. NOT uncensoring — removing safety data here is a controlled scientific ablation, not an effort to strip refusals, and the model's name must not be read as intent per rule 3.

WHAT THIS CHECKPOINT IS WORTH TO THE WITHIN-LINEAGE CONTRAST. Its sibling allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-SFT is the same base, same lab, same recipe, same step, with the three safety sets present. That is the AmberChat/AmberSafe shape the pass is looking for — one lineage, one lab, one base, safety data the only thing that moves — except it sits at the SFT step and the direction is subtractive (safety removed from a mix that had it) rather than additive (safety-only DPO added). One caution carried from this repo's own CLAUDE.md, docket [5260].3: allenai never released a DPO built on any ablated SFT, so this ablation has no downstream preference rung of its own, and any base→superego pairing of it inherits the FULL-mix DPO. The clean contrast exists at the SFT step only.

NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B.notes:
The MODEL CARD never names SFT or DPO — on the card alone method would be unknown. All method/algorithm/token/direction claims here come from the Hermes 3 Technical Report (arXiv:2408.11857), which the card explicitly points to. I string-matched every quote against the raw arXiv HTML. METHOD CHOICE: the released checkpoint is the product of SFT followed by a LoRA-adapter DPO stage; the report documents the two stages in separate sections (4.1 SFT, 4.2 DPO) but only one checkpoint is released, so I record the FINAL operation (dpo) rather than instruct_bundle. If the roster's convention is that a single checkpoint bundling SFT+DPO with no separate SFT release should be instruct_bundle, reclassify — the evidence supports either reading and the distinction is a convention, not a fact. DIRECTION: I have recorded "inverted", but flag the interpretive step honestly. The report never says it removed refusal data or used a toxic-DPO mixture; what it says is that the training data was built to make the model comply neutrally rather than refuse, and that guardrails belong at the system level, not in the weights: "We believe that a more appropriate place for guardrails and active intervention is at the larger system levels, rather than on the models themselves, which can result in an a priori lobotomization of potential lines of thinking. For Hermes, there is no such thing as latent thoughtcrime." The abstract's term is "a neutrally-aligned generalist instruct and tool use model". If the roster reserves "inverted" strictly for explicit de-censoring mixtures, this should be "standard" or "unknown". LICENSE ODDITY: frontmatter reads "license: llama3", not llama3.1, although the model is a Llama 3.1 derivative — quoted exactly as written. The card's base_model field names "meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B", the root repo's former name.

[attest-post-training-rungs-2026-08-16] FILE LIST CHECKED AND IT IS EMPTY OF RECIPES. /tree/main holds only .gitattributes, README.md, config.json, generation_config.json, 4 safetensors shards + index, special_tokens_map.json, tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json. Verified independently against the HF API (`?full=true` siblings) because the tree renderer can hide subdirectories — there is no configs/, no axolotl YAML, no trainer_state.json. cardData has no `datasets:` field. So every quantitative claim below comes from the Hermes 3 Technical Report (arXiv:2408.11857), which the card points to.

STAGE STRUCTURE (this is the field that matters for a within-lineage contrast). Base is meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B — the BASE, not Instruct (API tag `base_model:finetune:meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B`). Then SFT on the 390M-token mixture, then DPO: "When applying DPO rather than tuning a full model we train a LoRA adapter which side-steps the need to hold both a reference and trained model in GPU memory." DPO was kept at 8B — "Overall, DPO provided a moderate but positive impact on benchmarks" — while "For the larger model sizes DPO provided only a negligible performance improvements and thus we chose rather to remain with the SFT-phase checkpoints." CAVEAT I could not resolve: the report does not state whether this released 8B repo is the SFT or the SFT+DPO checkpoint, and no separate -SFT/-DPO repos exist. Treat the DPO stage as run-but-not-separately-released.

WHY safety_data = absent, NOT unknown. A full mix IS stated (Table 1, 8 categories, 100.0%), and safety is not among them. I searched the report text for safety, harmless, harmful, red team, toxic, PKU, HH-RLHF, Anthropic, uncensored, unaligned, jailbreak — NONE appear. The word "safe" occurs zero times as a safety term. The absence is affirmative, not incidental: "We believe that a more appropriate place for guardrails and active intervention is at the larger system levels, rather than on the models themselves, which can result in an *a priori* lobotomization of potential lines of thinking. For Hermes, there is no such thing as latent thoughtcrime." And: "This distinguishes Hermes from popular closed weight commercial models, which may refuse instructions on moral grounds."

THE TRAP I CHECKED (rule 3). The mixture contains a category literally called "Steering and Alignment" at 2.5% / 10M tokens. This is NOT safety data. "Alignment" here is alignment TO THE USER: the card's ethos is "focused on aligning LLMs to the user, with powerful steering capabilities and control given to the end user," and the report says "our training data strongly encourages the model to follow the system and instruction prompts *exactly* and neutrally." Residual uncertainty, stated plainly: the report gives no description of that category's contents, so 2.5% of the mix is a named-but-undescribed box. If safety data existed anywhere it would have to hide there, and everything else in the paper argues it does not.

WHY mixed, NOT helpfulness. The abstract sentence evidences two intents at once — helpfulness ("generalist instruct and tool use model") and reasoning ("strong reasoning and creative abilities", supported by Math at 6.7% and by "we train on a diverse class of synthetically-created reasoning tasks"). A third strand sits close to `uncensoring` but I declined to label it that: `uncensoring` means deliberately REMOVING refusals, and Hermes 3 is trained from the base model, so it never had refusals to strip — it declines to instil them. Deliberate omission, not removal. That distinction is recorded here rather than forced into the enum.

VALUE FOR THE WITHIN-LINEAGE CONTRAST: this is a clean no-safety arm on meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B, the same base as llama/tulu/tulu-no-safety in this repo's battery. Against meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct it gives one base, two labs, safety-present vs safety-absent — weaker than the AmberChat/AmberSafe shape (lab differs), but the base is held fixed.

NEVER ESTIMATED: no proportion here is derived. The one named dataset (hermes-function-calling-v1) has no stated share — it plausibly feeds the 4.3% Tool Use category, but the report does not say so and I did not assign it. Its card states ~10.68k examples across subsets, which is a dataset size, not a share of the mix.

CAUTION ON THE HTML: arxiv.org/html/2507.22448v1 truncates via WebFetch exactly at §4.1–4.3, and a summariser reading the truncated version will report "no post-training details given". That is a fetch artefact, not the paper. I downloaded the raw HTML (2.1 MB) and read §4 directly.

STRUCTURE: "we detail the two-stage post-training procedure for our Falcon-H1 models, which consists of Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) followed by Offline Reinforcement Learning." The offline RL stage is DPO: "we utilized a fork of the AllenAI open-instruct repository... our data mixture was built upon Tulu3... We employed the standard DPO loss function (dpo_loss_type: dpo_norm)."

INTENT = mixed, on one sentence evidencing two categories: reasoning ("complex reasoning, mathematical and scientific problem-solving") and helpfulness ("instruction-following, and function calling", plus the bullet "We enhanced the model's conversational abilities and instruction-following by improving personalization, stylistic variety and multi-round long conversation capability"). Counterweight worth recording: the release blog states "The current Falcon-H1 models were trained without reasoning-specific fine-tuning" — i.e. no thinking/CoT-mode tuning. I read that as excluding a reasoning MODE, not contradicting math/science problem-solving as a stated SFT objective; a stricter reader could downgrade this to helpfulness alone.

SAFETY = unknown, and this is a genuine unresolved, not a shrug. The word "safety" appears ZERO times in the entire technical report; "harmless", "refusal", "red-team", "jailbreak" are also zero. The only toxicity work described is a PRETRAINING filter ("A rule-based toxicity filter was applied using human-curated lists of offensive words"), which is out of scope here. So TII names no safety dataset. BUT a mix IS stated, and its single largest named component — Tulu3 at ~50% weight — ships safety data by its own card: CoCoNot (10,983 prompts), Tulu 3 WildGuardMix (50,000), Tulu 3 WildJailbreak (50,000), within 939,344 samples. The report says only that they "partially adopted and refined the datasets such as OpenMathInstruct-2, Tulu3, Smoltalk, and hermes-function-calling-v1" — "partially adopted" leaves it unstated whether the safety subsets were among the parts adopted. "present" would be an inference from a transitive dependency; "absent" would be false given that dependency. Hence unknown. If a downstream analysis needs this resolved, the discriminator is which Tulu3 subsets were kept, and no opened source states it.

SHARES: only one proportion is stated anywhere (Tulu3 ~50% of the SFT mixture, ~3.5 epochs; "The other data sources were repeated for fewer than 2 epochs"). Every other share is "unknown" as stated — none estimated. Note the 50% is a MIXTURE WEIGHT with repetition, not a share of unique examples.

method=sft is an inference from "fine-tuned ... on the data of GPT-JT" over a labelled NLP-task corpus; the card never writes "supervised fine-tuning" and never names an alignment algorithm, hence confidence medium and algorithm=unknown. DATASET DETAIL from the linked dataset card (secondary to this checkpoint): RedPajama-Data-Instruct is "curated from a diverse collection of NLP tasks from both [P3 (BigScience)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/bigscience/P3) and [Natural Instruction (AI2)](https://github.com/allenai/natural-instructions)" with HELM decontamination that "filtered out 137 tasks and 5.2M instances (out of 1069 tasks and 93.3M instances)". STAGE: this is a single SFT rung. base (RedPajama-INCITE-7B-Base, 1.001T tokens) → Instruct (1B tokens of instruction fine-tuning). There is no preference stage anywhere in this checkpoint — no DPO, no PPO, no reward model, no preference dataset named on any page I opened.

WHY absent RATHER THAN unknown: a mix IS stated, and it is stated at file granularity. The card's frontmatter declares `togethercomputer/RedPajama-Data-Instruct`, and that dataset repo contains exactly two data files — P3_decontaminated and NI_decontaminated. THE MISUSE SECTION IS NOT SAFETY DATA. The card has a long "Misuse, Malicious Use, and Out-of-Scope Use" section ("Using the model to generate content that is cruel to individuals is a misuse of this model", "Promoting hate speech, discrimination, or violence…"). This is a use policy addressed to the end user — "It is the responsibility of the end user to ensure that the model is used in a responsible and ethical manner" — not a description of training data or a training objective. It is boilerplate shared verbatim with the Base card. It must not be scored as safety intent; doing so would be exactly the "don't infer intent from the word aligned" failure in a different costume.

ONE HEDGE, DECLARED. The card says the fine-tune used "the data of GPT-JT". GPT-JT's own card enumerates its mixture as "5% of COT, 20% of P3, 20% of NI, and 55% of the Pile". Those percentages are GPT-JT's, on GPT-JT's page, for GPT-JT's 0.92B-token run — they are NOT restated for this checkpoint, and I have not carried them over as this model's shares. Note the tension I could not resolve from sources: the declared artifact RedPajama-Data-Instruct holds only P3 and NI, while "the data of GPT-JT" would also include CoT and a 55% Pile replay. I listed CoT with that ambiguity flagged in its share string and left the Pile out of the dataset list as a pretraining corpus, but if a large fraction of this 1B-token fine-tune was in fact Pile replay, that is material to reading this rung as an "instruction" stage at all. Unresolved on the evidence available.

BEARING ON THE WITHIN-LINEAGE CONTRAST YOU ARE BUILDING: this lineage does NOT have the AmberChat/AmberSafe shape. Together released two siblings off the same RedPajama-INCITE-7B-Base — Instruct (this one: P3+NI, few-shot) and Chat (blog: "fine-tuned using data from Dolly 2.0 and Open Assistant"). Both middle rungs are helpfulness-only; neither branch introduces a safety dataset, so there is no step within this lineage where safety data is the only thing that changes. I read the field as asking whether safety data is in the mix (it is, on the authors' own statement) rather than whether a citable dataset card exists (it does not). METHOD CAVEAT WORTH RECORDING: my first WebFetch of the arXiv HTML returned fluent, plausible, WRONG "quotes" — e.g. "We apply Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to further align models with human preferences and improve instruction-following capabilities," which appears nowhere in the paper. I re-pulled the HTML with curl, stripped tags locally, and grepped. Everything quoted here is from that local text of https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22448v1. Any attestation on this roster built on a summarizer's paraphrase should be re-checked the same way.

INTENT = mixed, on one sentence that names both. §4.1 states the objective as "complex reasoning, mathematical and scientific problem-solving" (reasoning) AND "instruction-following, and function calling" (helpfulness), with three bulleted improvement areas: Mathematical Problem-Solving, Scientific Problem-Solving, and "Conversational and Instruction-Following: We enhanced the model's conversational abilities and instruction-following by improving personalization, stylistic variety and multi-round long conversation capability." Safety, harmlessness, refusals, red-teaming and jailbreaks are named NOWHERE in §4 — a case-insensitive grep for safety|harmless|harmful|toxic|refus|red.team|jailbreak|guard over the whole paper returns only pretraining-side hits, the relevant one being a pretraining web-data filter ("A rule-based toxicity filter was applied using human-curated lists of offensive words"), which is corpus curation before the base model, not post-training.

TENSION FLAGGED, NOT RESOLVED: the blog says verbatim "The current Falcon-H1 models were trained without reasoning-specific fine-tuning, yet they already demonstrate strong general instruction-following capabilities" (https://falcon-lm.github.io/blog/falcon-h1/). I read that as disclaiming a thinking/CoT-RL stage rather than contradicting §4.1's math-and-science SFT focus, but a reader who takes it at face value would downgrade this to helpfulness. Both quotes are supplied so the call can be re-made.

WHY safety_data = unknown AND NOT absent. This is the load-bearing judgement. Tulu3 is ~50% of the SFT mixture, and allenai/tulu-3-sft-mixture (939,344 samples, 18 sources) demonstrably contains three safety components: CoCoNot (10,983 prompts), Tulu 3 WildGuardMix (50,000), Tulu 3 WildJailbreak (50,000). But Falcon-H1 says it "partially adopted and refined the datasets such as" Tulu3 — "partially" and "such as" both do work here. Partial adoption means the safety subsets may or may not have been taken; "such as" means the list is not exhaustive; and the mix additionally includes unnamed proprietary data plus, at DPO, "several other open-source and in-house preference datasets." So no safety dataset is named in Falcon's own mix statement (which forbids `present`), and the mix as stated is not complete enough to have excluded one (which forbids `absent`). The DPO side is weaker evidence still: the Tulu3 preference mixture (272,898 generation pairs) lists no explicitly safety-labelled component. If this checkpoint's safety status is load-bearing for the roster, it needs TII to be asked directly — it is not recoverable from published sources.

SCOPE: the report describes post-training for the whole Falcon-H1 family; nothing in §4 is specific to the 1.5B checkpoint, except that the 128k long-context SFT stage was omitted only for the 0.5B model, so the 1.5B did receive both 3GT stages. The paper frames the pipeline as "Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) followed by Offline Reinforcement Learning," the offline RL being DPO run on "a fork of the AllenAI open-instruct repository" with "dpo_loss_type: dpo_norm", beta=5, stopped at ~1 epoch.

ONE DATASET DELIBERATELY OMITTED from the list: AceMath (Liu et al. 2024e) appears only as "Inspired by OpenMathInstruct-2 and AceMath, we synthesized math problems across diverse sub-domains" — inspiration for synthesis, not an adopted corpus. The four in the list are the ones under "we partially adopted and refined."

ContextualAI/archangel_sft_pythia2-8b.notes:
This is the SFT stage the four alignment arms build on, and it is itself released, which is why released_base is "yes" for the siblings. The card names the base only as "pythia2-8b", which does NOT disambiguate EleutherAI/pythia-2.8b from EleutherAI/pythia-2.8b-deduped; only the sft-ppo card in this set gives the full HF id. The card also documents conditional-SFT control tokens: "For models trained with our conditional SFT model, the tokenizers have additional tokens `<|good|>` and `<|bad|>` included in the embeddings." — that is about the CSFT variant's tokenizer, not a statement that THIS checkpoint is CSFT, so I did not score method from it. No token or example count anywhere on the card; the 169k/386k/88.8k row counts visible on the HF page come from the dataset viewer sidebar, not from the card text, so they are not booked as train_tokens.

[attest-post-training-rungs-2026-08-16] The HF repo file list has NO training configs (only weights, config.json, tokenizer files), so the model card's link to github.com/ContextualAI/HALOs is the only route to the mix. Current `main` there is a 2024+ rewrite; the archangel-era code is on the **`legacy` branch**, found via the branches API. That branch contains the exact script that produced this checkpoint.

EXACT PRODUCING COMMAND, verbatim from `scripts/populate_sbatch.sh` on `legacy` (exp_name is literally `archangel_${loss}_${model}` = `archangel_sft_pythia2-8b`, and the model list includes `pythia2-8b`, the loss list includes `sft`):
  `python train.py loss="$loss" model="$model" datasets=[shp,hh,oasst] exp_name="$exp_name" mode=train ...`

SAFETY DATA — the load-bearing detail, and it is only visible in the code. The dataset name passed is bare `hh`, not `hh_helpful`. In `legacy/dataloader.py`, `get_hh` has flags `only_helpful` / `only_harmless`, documented verbatim as "- only_helpful: only the helpfulness data" and "- only_harmless: only the harmlessness data", and separate `get_hh_helpful` / `get_hh_harmless` entry points exist. Bare `hh` takes neither flag, hitting the `else` branch verbatim:
  `dataset = datasets.load_dataset('Anthropic/hh-rlhf', split=split)`
  `data = Dataset('Anthropic-HH')`
i.e. the FULL hh-rlhf including harmless-base. The producers had a helpfulness-only option and did not use it. The dataset card for Anthropic/hh-rlhf describes it as "Human preference data about helpfulness and harmlessness from Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback." Hence safety_data=present and intent=mixed (helpfulness via SHP/OASST/HH-helpful, harmlessness via HH-harmless) — NOT inferred from the word "aligned" in the card, which I disregarded per the rules.

How safety data reaches an SFT (not preference) checkpoint: `get_hh`'s docstring says verbatim "For this dataset, the SFT text is the preferred response.", and `SFTDataLoader` trains on `example.generations[example.sft_index]`. So on harmless-base prompts the target is the more-harmless response. (Contrast SHP, where the docstring says the SFT text is just "the first response" because "the absolute best response cannot be inferred from SHP".)

SHARES: none stated anywhere. The three per-dataset row counts visible in HF's sidebar (SHP 386k, hh-rlhf 169k, oasst1 88.8k) are full dataset sizes, not stated shares of this mix, and HALOs uses train splits only — so I recorded "unknown" rather than passing them off as shares.

CAUTION FOR THE WITHIN-LINEAGE CONTRAST THIS PASS IS BUILDING. The archangel suite does NOT have the AmberChat/AmberSafe shape. Every archangel variant — `sft`, `csft`, `dpo`, `kto`, `ppo`, `slic`, and the `sft+X` chains — is trained on the identical `datasets=[shp,hh,oasst]`; the two loops in populate.sh/populate_sbatch.sh vary only `loss` and `model`. The `sft+X` variants additionally load `archangel_sft_${model}/LATEST/policy.pt` as their starting point, so within this lineage the SFT rung is the parent and the preference rungs change the LOSS ONLY, with data held constant. So archangel supports a within-lineage OBJECTIVE contrast, not a safety-data contrast, and it cannot serve as an unsafety/safety pair.

Base is confirmed `EleutherAI/pythia-2.8b` from both `config.json` (`_name_or_path`) and `legacy/config/model/pythia2-8b.yaml` (`name_or_path: EleutherAI/pythia-2.8b`) — note the repo name says "2-8b" but this is 2.8B, not 2 to 8 B.

The recipe lives in the linked code repo, ContextualAI/HALOs, on its **legacy** branch (main has since been rewritten for ultrabin/Llama-3 and no longer describes Archangel).

So the SFT parent (ContextualAI/archangel_sft_pythia2-8b, "optimized with the loss **SFT**", same three datasets) was trained on `datasets=[shp,hh,oasst]`, and the KTO step was run on `datasets=[shp,hh,oasst]` too. This is offline preference optimisation from a binary desirable/undesirable signal — no rollouts, no reward model — so I filed both dataset passes as stage `preference` rather than `rl`.

SAFETY DATA — the point the file list decides. `hh` is not a helpfulness-only slice. `dataloader.py` (legacy) defines `get_hh(..., only_helpful=False, only_harmless=False)`; the flags exist (`data_dir="helpful-base"` / `data_dir="harmless-base"`, giving dataset names `hh_helpful` / `hh_harmless`) but the driver passes plain `hh`, which takes the default branch `datasets.load_dataset('Anthropic/hh-rlhf', split=split)` with `dataset_name = 'hh'`. The dataset card documents that default explicitly: "# Load all helpfulness/harmless subsets (share the same schema)". So Anthropic's harmlessness preference data (harmless-base) is in the mix at BOTH stages. The red-team subset is NOT (it needs `data_dir="red-team-attempts"`). Hence `present`.

INTENT — mixed, both halves evidenced, and neither is a name inference. Helpfulness: SHP is Reddit helpfulness preferences ("385K collective human preferences over responses to questions/instructions in 18 different subject areas"), OASST is assistant-quality conversations. Harmlessness: harmless-base as above, plus the paper's evaluation criterion, verbatim from https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.01306v4 — "We use GPT-4-0613 to judge whether the aligned model's response is better than the SFT target for a given test input with respect to helpfulness, harmlessness, and conciseness". The blog framing quoted in intent_quote names the two dimensions as the suite's research question.

CAVEAT ON HOW MUCH WEIGHT THIS BEARS FOR A WITHIN-LINEAGE CONTRAST. Archangel is NOT an AmberChat/AmberSafe-shaped pair. The whole 56-model suite is a loss-function ablation: "Archangel comprises 56 models in total: 7 different sizes from 1B to 30B aligned with 8 different methods on 3 of the largest public human feedback datasets", and the paper states "All models are aligned under identical settings on the same data, save for hyperparameters unique to them." The variable that changes across the suite is the LOSS (sft, dpo, kto, ppo, slic, csft, and the sft+X two-stage variants), not the data — the mix is `[shp,hh,oasst]` everywhere. Within this lineage, `archangel_sft_pythia2-8b` → `archangel_sft-kto_pythia2-8b` holds the data fixed and changes only the objective, so the base→SFT→KTO ladder here CANNOT isolate safety data; safety data (harmless-base) is present at every rung including the SFT one. The clean contrasts this suite supports are loss-vs-loss, not safety-vs-no-safety.

SHARES: no proportion is stated anywhere for how shp/hh/oasst combine, so every share is unknown; the per-dataset totals I appended are the dataset cards' own totals, not mix shares, and are labelled as such. ContextualAI/archangel_sft-ppo_pythia2-8.notes: THREE-WAY DISCREPANCY, and the reason this checkpoint deserves separate handling. (1) The repo id is `archangel_sft-ppo_...`, implying SFT then PPO. (2) The CARD drops the SFT prefix that all four sibling cards carry: "- optimized with the loss PPO" (siblings read SFT+DPO / SFT+KTO / SFT+SLIC). (3) The PAPER labels this pipeline with the prefix restored and the variant marked: its sample-generation table row is "SFT+PPO (offline)", and the method section says "for a fair comparison with offline methods, we consider a variant of PPO that is only fed offline data." I booked method from the card (ppo) and the offline qualifier as a separate algorithm claim from the paper. Do not record this as standard online RLHF-PPO: the paper states it never updates the old policy ("we never update πold and keep it as πref") and uses dummy ±1 rewards rather than a learned reward model. Two further card-level oddities: this card alone names the base with its full HF id (EleutherAI/pythia-2.8b, so this one is unambiguously the non-deduped root), and this card alone omits the `<|good|>`/`<|bad|>` conditional-SFT paragraph. [attest-post-training-rungs-2026-08-16] FILE LIST CHECKED, AND IT IS BARE: /tree/main holds only .gitattributes, README.md, config.json, generation_config.json, two safetensors shards + index, and tokenizer files. No configs/, no training YAML, no trainer_state.json. The recipe therefore had to be traced to the code repo the card names. Two-stage, both stages on the SAME mix. Card (raw README, verbatim): "This repo contains the model checkpoints for: - model family EleutherAI/pythia-2.8b - optimized with the loss PPO - aligned using the SHP, Anthropic HH and Open Assistant datasets." Paper (arxiv.org/pdf/2402.01306v4): "The models are trained on a combination of Anthropic-HH (Ganguli et al., 2022), OpenAssistant (Köpf et al., 2023), and SHP (Ethayarajh et al., 2022). All models are aligned under identical settings on the same data, save for hyperparameters unique to them. Similar to Rafailov et al. (2023), the target sequences for SFT are a subset of {y_w}." The `sft-` prefix is the SFT stage; SFT data is the chosen responses of those same three preference sets, so I listed all three at both stages. Legacy README's worked commands confirm the dataset list is passed identically to both: `python train.py loss=sft model=llama7b datasets=[shp,hh,oasst] ...` then `python train.py loss=kto model=llama7b datasets=[shp,hh,oasst] ... ++model.load_from=llama7b_sft/LATEST/policy.pt`. STAGE 2 IS NOT ONLINE RLHF. Paper: "PPO is an online algorithm... However, for a fair comparison with offline methods, we consider a variant of PPO that is only fed offline data." Legacy README: "PPO (offline, off-policy variant)". config/loss/ppo.yaml sets `trainer: PPOTrainer`, `dataloader: UnpairedPreferenceDataLoader`, `KL_coef: 0.1`. I coded it `rl` (PPO-Clip objective with critic and KL penalty), but it consumes offline preference data, so `preference` is defensible too — flagging rather than hiding the judgement call. SAFETY DATA IS PRESENT BUT NOT SEPARABLE, AND NOT AIMED AT. `safety_data: present` rests on a code fact, not the card: legacy dataloader.py `get_hh` is called without `only_harmless`/`only_helpful` under `datasets=[shp,hh,oasst]`, and that branch is `datasets.load_dataset('Anthropic/hh-rlhf', split=split)` with NO `data_dir` — i.e. the whole of hh-rlhf, whose card describes "Human preference data about helpfulness and harmlessness". The harmless-base subset is in the mix. But the loader HAS `only_harmless=True` (`data_dir="harmless-base"`) as an unused option here, so the harmlessness portion was available to isolate and was not isolated. No share is stated anywhere for any of the three datasets, at either stage, and none is estimable — hh-rlhf's 161k train rows is a dataset size, not a mix proportion. post_training_size is likewise unstated. Intent `mixed` on the evaluation criterion quote plus the impact statement ("The methods discussed in this paper have the potential to make LLMs more helpful and safer"). Both helpfulness and harmlessness are evidenced, neither is the stated objective — the paper's actual aim is loss-function comparison (HALOs vs non-HALOs), which the enum has no slot for. If the gate wants the narrowest reading, `helpfulness` is the fallback; `safety` would be wrong. BEARING ON THE WITHIN-LINEAGE CONTRAST THIS PASS IS FOR — this rung does NOT have the AmberChat/AmberSafe shape. The archangel suite varies the LOSS (sft, sft-dpo, sft-ppo, sft-kto, sft-slic, and the loss-from-base variants) while holding the data mix fixed: "All models are aligned under identical settings on the same data." So archangel_sft vs archangel_sft-ppo isolates the objective, with safety data constant and present at both. There is no step in this lineage where safety data is the only thing that changes, and no archangel arm trained on a safety corpus alone. Any within-lineage safety contrast built on this family would be confounded with the loss function — which is, however, exactly what makes it a clean control for the OPPOSITE question.

Quoted the card form verbatim as required. The paper also notes its SLiC implementation deviates from the original: "Instead of sampling from the reference model to calculate the Lreg as Zhao et al. (2023) do—as it is very slow—we just apply the cross-entropy loss to the SFT data" — so "SLiC" here is a modified reimplementation, worth flagging if the roster treats method labels as interchangeable across papers. The recipe lives in the linked code repo (github.com/ContextualAI/HALOs), which has since been rewritten; the Archangel-era state is at commit 83d93ee (Jan 2024). scripts/populate.sh there is the producer of this exact checkpoint: losses=("sft" "sft+csft" "sft+dpo" "sft+kto" "sft+ppo" "sft+slic" ...), models=(... "pythia2-8b" ...), and for a "sft+" loss it runs `python train.py loss="$alignment_loss" model="$model" datasets=[shp,hh,oasst] exp_name="$exp_name" mode=train ++cache_dir="$cache_dir" ++model.load_from="$sft_model"` where sft_model="archangel_sft_${model}/LATEST/policy.pt". So BOTH stages use the SAME three-dataset mix: stage 1 = SFT (loss/sft.yaml, SFTDataLoader) on shp+hh+oasst, stage 2 = SLiC (loss/slic.yaml, name: slic, trainer: SLiCTrainer, dataloader: PairedPreferenceDataLoader, beta 1.0, lambda_coef 0.1, use_reference_model: false) resumed from the SFT policy on the same shp+hh+oasst. This checkpoint therefore does NOT have the AmberChat/AmberSafe shape — the preference step adds no safety data that the SFT step lacked, so there is no within-lineage safety-only contrast at this rung. WHY safety_data=present: dataloader.py `get_hh` loads the FULL dataset when the name is plain `hh` (as populate.sh passes): `dataset = datasets.load_dataset('Anthropic/hh-rlhf', split=split)`; the helpful-only and harmless-only paths (data_dir="helpful-base" / "harmless-base", registered as `get_hh_helpful` / `get_hh_harmless`) are NOT what the Archangel command invokes. The full load includes harmless-base, i.e. Anthropic's harmlessness/red-team preference data. The loader docstring also fixes the SFT stage's targets: "For this dataset, the SFT text is the preferred response." Note the HH card's own warning that these data "are *not* meant for supervised training of dialogue agents" — Archangel trains SFT on them anyway. Intent = mixed on two independent legs, both evidenced: (a) harmlessness data is in the mix via full hh-rlhf (quote above); (b) the HALOs technical report (assets/report.pdf at the same commit) states the evaluation criterion — "Then we used GPT-4 to judge whether the aligned model's response was better than the human-chosen response in the data (i.e., 𝑦𝑤) for the given context 𝑥 on the basis of helpfulness, harmlessness, and conciseness." The report's own framing of the release is methodological rather than safety-motivated: "To validate KTO and understand how alignment scales across model sizes, we are releasing Archangel, the largest-ever suite of human-feedback aligned LLMs. It comprises 56 models: {7 pretrained models from 1B to 30B} x {8 different alignment methods}, all aligned on a mixture of the Anthropic HH (Ganguli et al., 2022), Stanford Human Preferences (Ethayarajh et al., 2022), and OpenAssistant (Köpf et al., 2023) datasets under nearly identical training settings." THE STAGE SPLIT IS THE POINT HERE, AND IT CUTS THE OTHER WAY FROM AmberChat/AmberSafe. Safety data sits at the SFT rung, not the DPO rung:
 - SFT mixture: wildguardmixtrain 50,000 + wildjailbreak 49,965 + coconot 10,835 = 110,800 of 866,138 rows (12.8%) are safety/noncompliance sources.
 - DPO mixture: 9 source labels, ENUMERATED IN FULL above, and not one is a safety, red-team, harmlessness or jailbreak set. The card's own bullets name only WildChat, Ultrafeedback, DaringAnteater, instruction-following personas and reused SFT prompts.
So this lineage is the INVERSE of Amber: safety enters at SFT and the preference step adds none. I set safety_data=present because the field asks whether safety is named anywhere in this checkpoint's post-training mix and the card explicitly makes the SFT mixture part of this model's pipeline. If your contrast wants the DELTA AT THE DPO STEP ALONE, the answer there is absent, on a stated and fully enumerated mix.

ONE CAVEAT I CANNOT CLOSE. Three DPO sources are reused SFT prompts (olmo2-1b-sft-used-p1/p2-on-policy, olmo2-1b-sft-if = 183,293 rows, 48% of the mix). The SFT prompt pool they were drawn from contains the 110,800 safety rows, so some safety prompts may well have been re-used into the preference mix. Neither card says whether safety prompts were included or filtered out, and the `source` labels are aggregated so they cannot be counted. That is unknown, not absent.

INTENT. The only objective sentence on the card is the Tülu 3 one quoted above — benchmark/task quality (MATH, GSM8K, IFEval), safety not among the stated aims. I read that as helpfulness rather than mixed or reasoning: MATH/GSM8K appear as benchmarks in a list of "a diversity of tasks", not as a stated chain-of-thought objective, and nothing on the card states a safety goal. The card in fact disclaims one: "The OLMo-2 models have limited safety training, but are not deployed automatically with in-the-loop filtering of responses like ChatGPT, so the model can produce problematic outputs (especially when prompted to do so)." Consistent with that, the card's own Safety benchmark column FALLS across this step — OLMo 2 1B SFT 93.2 → OLMo 2 1B DPO 89.9 — while IFEval rises 50.5 → 67.1 and AlpacaEval 2 LC rises 2.4 → 9.5. The measured direction matches a preference stage aimed at instruction-following and chat quality, not at harmlessness.

Two smaller things worth flagging. (1) The DPO dataset card is partly COPY-PASTED FROM THE 32B: it says "This preference mixture used for DPO on our the OLMo-2-0325-32B-SFT checkpoint to obtain OLMo-2-0325-32B-DPO", yet the repo is the 1B mix and its source labels are all `olmo2-1b-*`. The 32B sentence is stale text, not evidence about this checkpoint. (2) The card's "Intermediate Checkpoints" section says weights were "saved every 20 training steps ... during the model's RLVR training" and gives `revision="step_200"` — RLVR wording on a DPO repo, most likely another paste-through from the Instruct card. I did not treat it as evidence of an RL stage in this checkpoint, and listed no `rl` stage.

allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct.notes:
TWO THINGS THE ROSTER PROBABLY HAS WRONG. (1) PARENT: Instruct is NOT trained from the DPO checkpoint. Its card names allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B-RLVR1 as the parent, and RLVR1 is itself a separate released RLVR stage on top of DPO: RLVR1's card says 'OLMo 2 1B RLVR 1 April 2025 is post-trained variant of the [allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B-DPO](https://huggingface.co/allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B-DPO) model, which has undergone supervised finetuning on an OLMo-specific variant of the [Tülu 3 dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/tulu-3-sft-olmo-2-mixture-0225), further DPO training on [this dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/olmo-2-0425-1b-preference-mix), and final RLVR training on [this dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/RLVR-GSM-MATH-IF-Mixed-Constraints).' So there are two RLVR stages on different mixtures (RLVR-GSM-MATH-IF-Mixed-Constraints, then RLVR-MATH), and a DPO->Instruct edge silently skips a released checkpoint. RLVR1 is public (HTTP 200 unauthenticated), hence released_base 'yes'. (2) ALGORITHM: GRPO -- and this is exactly why the schema separates algorithm from method. At 1B the RLVR optimiser is GRPO while the 7B and 13B of the same family use PPO; same table row: '| Post-training | SFT+DPO+GRPO
...| SFT + DPO + PPO
...| SFT + DPO + PPO
...| SFT + DPO + GRPO
...|' for 1B/7B/13B/32B. PROVENANCE CAVEAT: that GRPO string sits on the BASE model card's training table, not on the Instruct card; the Instruct card names no optimiser. reasoning 'unknown': RLVR-MATH is verifiable-reward math training, which is not documented chain-of-thought targeting, and no card in this lineage mentions CoT or a thinking mode. A would-be allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B-RLVR2 returns HTTP 401, i.e. not public. [attest-post-training-2026-08-16] TREE CHECKED, NOTHING THERE: /tree/main holds only .gitattributes, README.md, config.json, generation_config.json, merges.txt, model.safetensors, special_tokens_map.json, tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json, vocab.json — no training YAML, no trainer_state.json, no configs/. I also walked allenai/open-instruct configs/train_configs (dirs: dpo, olmo2, sft, tulu3); olmo2/ contains only 1124_7b/13b and 32b SFT/DPO YAMLs, nothing for the 0425 1B. So the evidence is the model card chain plus dataset cards. STAGE CHAIN (each link read on its own card): OLMo-2-0425-1B (base) → SFT on allenai/tulu-3-sft-olmo-2-mixture-0225 → DPO on allenai/olmo-2-0425-1b-preference-mix → RLVR on allenai/RLVR-GSM-MATH-IF-Mixed-Constraints = OLMo-2-0425-1B-RLVR1 → a SECOND RLVR run on allenai/RLVR-MATH = this checkpoint. The Instruct card's frontmatter lists only `datasets: [allenai/RLVR-MATH]` and `base_model: [allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B-RLVR1]`; the earlier RLVR dataset is recoverable only from the RLVR1 card, which is why it is listed here. WHY `mixed`, with the pieces separately evidenced: (a) safety — the SFT mix carries three named safety/refusal sets, WildGuardMix, WildJailbreak and CoCoNot, and the model card itself concedes "limited safety training" and prints a "Safety" eval column (SFT 93.2, DPO 89.9, final 87.6, i.e. safety score falls across post-training); (b) helpfulness — "Tülu 3 is designed for state-of-the-art performance on a diversity of tasks in addition to chat"; (c) reasoning — both RL stages are verifiable-reward math/GSM/IF. SHARE PROVENANCE, read this before quoting the SFT subset counts: the 0225 mixture card gives NO component list — it is defined by an open-instruct `update_subsets.py` command against allenai/tulu-3-sft-olmo-2-mixture-filter-datecutoff. The per-subset counts I report are `source`-column value counts from the HF dataset-viewer statistics endpoint on the 0225 mix itself (they sum to 866,138 = the card's num_examples). The 50,000 / 50,000 / 10,983 prompt figures are the PARENT card's (allenai/tulu-3-sft-olmo-2-mixture, 939,344 samples) and differ slightly from the shipped mix because of date-cutoff filtering and the math-subset swap. Both are stated numbers; neither is estimated; do not mix the denominators. DPO STAGE HAS NO NAMED SAFETY SUBSET. The preference-mix card lists seven on-policy sources and the viewer's `source` counts give nine: olmo2-1b-sft-used-p2-on-policy 97,642; olmo2-1b-wildchat-unused-on-policy 84,208; olmo2-1b-sft-if 65,876; olmo2-1b-ultrafeedback-cleaned 60,819; tulu-3-pref-personas-instruction-following 19,890; olmo2-1b-sft-used-p1-on-policy 19,775; olmo2-1b-wildchat-used-on-policy 17,678; olmo2-1b-wildchat-if 10,795; olmo2-1b-daring-anteater 1,618. Safety prompts may ride along inside the reused SFT prompts, but no card says so — treat DPO-stage safety content as unknown, not absent-by-design. Also worth flagging for the roster: this preference mix's own card says it "used for DPO on our the OLMo-2-0325-32B-SFT checkpoint" — the card is written for the 32B, and several sub-source names still say `-olmo32`, while the viewer shows `olmo2-1b-*` sources. The 1B mix is the on-policy regeneration; the card text was not fully updated. `safety_data: present` rests on the SFT stage alone, and it is a real presence, not a token one: ~110,800 of 866,138 SFT rows (WildGuardMix + WildJailbreak + CoCoNot) — which lines up with the ~5% figure this repo's CLAUDE.md books for OLMo 3 SFT only if you count CoCoNot alone; the WildJailbreak/WildGuardMix pair pushes the OLMo-2 1B SFT safety fraction an order of magnitude higher. Do not carry the OLMo 3 percentage over to this checkpoint.

BASE MODEL — the headline finding. The roster places this under Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B; both primary sources say Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B. direction "unknown" is deliberate. Nothing in the card or the paper states a direction for the DISTILLED checkpoints. The paper's helpfulness/harmlessness language ("a secondary reinforcement learning stage aimed at improving the model's helpfulness and harmlessness") describes R1's own second RL stage, not the distills, which received only SFT on R1 outputs. Attaching that quote here would be exactly the misfiling rule 1 warns about. There is no evidence of a de-censoring or refusal-removal objective either — absence of that evidence is not a finding.

LICENCE NUANCE (not a contradiction, but two licences are in play): frontmatter is "license: mit" and §7 licenses the weights MIT, while the same section states the Qwen-derived distills "are originally licensed under [Apache 2.0 License]". The card asserts MIT for the released artifact and acknowledges the upstream Apache-2.0 provenance; it does not resolve which governs a downstream user.

LAB FOR THIS CHECKPOINT is DeepSeek-AI (paper byline "DeepSeek-AI research@deepseek.com"), NOT the root's lab. The `lab` object in this report describes Qwen Team / Alibaba Cloud, who trained the root, per the task spec.

[attest-direction-2026-08-16] Post-training here is SFT distillation of Qwen2.5-Math-7B on reasoning traces from DeepSeek-R1, whose own pipeline the same card describes as incorporating "two RL stages aimed at discovering improved reasoning patterns and aligning with human preferences" — so the teacher's data is preference-aligned and nothing was stripped or optimised against. The repo ships no training YAML and names no datasets (files are only weights, config, tokenizer, LICENSE, README), and the card, HF tags and cardData contain no uncensoring or de-alignment claim; safety training is simply not emphasised, which is an absence, not inversion.

[attest-post-training-extra-2026-08-16] FILE LIST OPENED, AND IT IS BARE. /tree/main root holds only .gitattributes, LICENSE, README.md, config.json, generation_config.json, two safetensors shards + index, tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json, and a figures/ dir. No configs/, no training YAML, no trainer_state.json, no recipe. The card's README is the shared DeepSeek-R1 README, so the only substantive post-training statement is the paper's; I extracted the arXiv PDF locally with pdftotext and quoted from that text rather than from a summarizer.

STAGE IS THE LOAD-BEARING FIELD HERE AND IT IS SFT ONLY. Verbatim, same page as the intent quote: "For distilled models, we apply only SFT and do not include an RL stage, even though incorporating RL could substantially boost model performance." There is no preference/RL rung on this checkpoint at all.

WHY safety_data = absent RATHER THAN unknown, AND THE ONE GAP IN IT. The 800k mix IS stated and decomposed: "In total, we collect about 600k reasoning related training samples" and "we collected a total of approximately 200k training samples that are unrelated to reasoning", the latter enumerated by task type as "writing, factual QA, self-cognition, and translation". No safety, harmlessness, red-team or refusal dataset appears in that mix. Harmlessness in this paper lives entirely in a stage the distills did not get — §2.3.4: "we implement a secondary reinforcement learning stage aimed at improving the model's helpfulness and harmlessness", and later, confirming it is a real and separate thing, "its tendency to refuse answering certain queries after safety RL. Without safety RL, DeepSeek-R1 could achieve an accuracy of over 70%." That safety RL is on DeepSeek-R1 (the teacher), not on this 7B.
THE GAP, stated plainly so it is not mistaken for a clean absent: the 200k non-reasoning portion "reuse[s] portions of the SFT dataset of DeepSeek-V3", and that DeepSeek-V3 SFT set is not enumerated in this paper. If V3's SFT contained safety instances, some could ride along unnamed. So "absent" here means: no safety data is named anywhere in the stated mix, with an unenumerated inherited subset that I could not resolve from these sources. Treat it as absent-by-statement, not absent-by-audit.

FOR THE WITHIN-LINEAGE CONTRAST. This is a clean case of post-training aimed at reasoning with no safety rung — teacher-output SFT only, one step off Qwen2.5-Math-7B. Note the base: the paper says "The base models we use here are Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B, Qwen2.5-Math-7B, Qwen2.5-14B, Qwen2.5-32B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct" — so the 7B distill's parent is Qwen2.5-MATH-7B, not Qwen2.5-7B. If the roster attaches this rung to plain Qwen2.5-7B, the parentage is wrong and any within-lineage contrast built on it inherits the error. Also worth flagging for a contrast that pairs this against Qwen's own instruct rung: the teacher was safety-RL'd and this student was not, so any residual refusal behaviour here is distilled, not trained.

METHOD IS INFERRED FROM THE OPERATION, NOT THE NAME: neither the card nor the paper ever writes "SFT" for AmberChat. The card says "instruction following model finetuned from", the paper says "AmberChat is trained on the evolved instruct training data as used by WizardLM. We use FastChat to finetune the model for 3 epochs on 8 A100s (80G) distributed by FSDP, the learning rate is 2e-5, gradient accumulation steps is 16, warmup ratio is 0.04." Supervised instruction finetuning on instruction data with no preference signal = sft. The term "supervised fine-tuning (SFT)" appears in this lineage only on the AmberSafe card, quoting the DPO repo's procedure. CARD-vs-PAPER DATASET DISCREPANCY: card lists two sets (WizardLM evol-instruct 143k + share_gpt_90k 90k = 233k); the paper's method section names only WizardLM ("AmberChat is trained on the evolved instruct training data as used by WizardLM"), while the paper's results section says "we note that AmberChat simply trained on ShareGPT 90K also demonstrates much higher performance than our base model" -- i.e. the paper attributes AmberChat to WizardLM data in one place and ShareGPT in another. The card's two-dataset mix is the most complete statement and I take it as authoritative. direction=unknown: nothing in either source says anything about refusal behaviour in either direction; the datasets are ordinary instruction mixtures, but I am not scoring "standard" from the absence of de-censoring language. No named optimiser distinct from the operation, so no algorithm claim (FastChat is the training framework, not an optimiser). ID redirects to IFM/AmberChat.

[attest-direction-2026-08-16] Ordinary instruction tuning (WizardLM evol-instruct + ShareGPT, MT-Bench 5.43); no uncensoring claim anywhere in LLM360's materials, and LLM360 released AmberSafe separately as the safety-tuned checkpoint, so AmberChat's lack of safety data is an absence, not a reversal. One genuine complication, flagged rather than acted on: the card's DataMix table names icybee/share_gpt_90k_v1, but the finetuning code the card links loads `anon8231489123/ShareGPT_Vicuna_unfiltered` (prepare_evol_datamix.py), whose own card says "~100k ShareGPT conversations narrowed down to 53k by: ... Removing various instances 'AI Moralizing'" — a refusal-thinned corpus. It does not carry the direction here: the file loaded is `ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json`, which that card describes as the variant that RETAINS "I'm sorry, but" refusals (the no_imsorry file is the stripped one), and the stated intent is data cleaning for a Vicuna recipe, not de-censoring a model.

[attest-post-training-rungs-2026-08-16] STAGE: pure SFT. Instruction finetuning of LLM360/Amber with FastChat (`FastChat/fastchat/train/train_mem.py`, 3 epochs, lr 2e-5, 8xA100). No preference stage, no DPO, no RM. The /tree/main file list holds only weights, tokenizer and config — no training YAML — so the recipe was traced through the card's "Finetuning Code" link to github.com/LLM360/amber-train/finetune/amberchat, which contains the actual launch script and the datamix builder.

SAFETY: absent, on a stated and complete mix. The DataMix table totals 233k rows across exactly two instruction datasets and no safety/harmlessness set appears in it, in the launch script, or in the paper's description.

THE FILE-LIST PAYOFF — the mix is not merely safety-free, it is safety-SUBTRACTED. `prepare_evol_datamix.py` does not load the `icybee/share_gpt_90k_v1` named on the HF card; it loads `anon8231489123/ShareGPT_Vicuna_unfiltered`, `data_files="ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json"`. That dataset's card states it was built by "Removing various instances 'AI Moralizing'. Conversations with these phrases were removed" — the listed phrases include "inappropriate", "offensive", "illegal", "harmful", "hate speech", "responsible AI", "It is important to". So the SFT stage feeds Amber ShareGPT conversations with refusal and moralizing turns stripped out. I did NOT score this as `uncensoring` intent: rule 3 forbids reading the word "unfiltered" in a dataset name as a goal, LLM360 never states an uncensoring objective anywhere, and this is the standard Vicuna-replication corpus chosen for instruction quality (the stated target is MT-Bench, 2.49 -> 5.428125). The de-moralizing is a property of the data the lab inherited, not an aim it declared. Flagging it because it sharpens rather than weakens the "no safety at this rung" reading.

WITHIN-LINEAGE CONTRAST — CONFIRMED, and it is the clean shape this pass is looking for. `finetune/ambersafe/` (dpo.sh, get_saferlhf.py, sft.sh) sits beside `finetune/amberchat/` in the same repo, same lab, same base. finetune/README.md: "AmberSafe is a safety-finetuned instruction model using LLM360/AmberChat as the base. It's an aligned version of the model finetuned with Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)", DataMix "PKU-Alignment/PKU-SafeRLHF | 330k | Total | 330k", and "Since we focus on safety, we will need to filter out the rows with the same halmlessness annotation." AmberChat -> AmberSafe therefore isolates safety data as the only changing variable at that step.

DISCREPANCIES worth carrying (three sources disagree, none silently resolvable):
1. The 90k ShareGPT slot is named `icybee/share_gpt_90k_v1` on the HF card and `anon8231489123/ShareGPT_Vicuna_unfiltered` in both the GitHub DataMix table and the executable loader. I listed both entries so neither is dropped, but they are ONE 90k slot — do not sum to 180k. The code is the stronger evidence.
2. The paper (ar5iv 2312.06550) says only "AmberChat is trained on the evolved instruct training data as used by WizardLM [36]", omitting ShareGPT entirely, and later "we note that AmberChat simply trained on ShareGPT 90K also demonstrates much higher performance than our base model" — which reads as a separate ablation, not the released checkpoint.
3. The paper attributes AmberSafe's DPO to a base of "checkpoint 355 instead of the last checkpoint" and to "ShareGPT 90K ... further optimized on the SafeRLHF dataset", while the repo README says AmberSafe's base is AmberChat and the mix is PKU-SafeRLHF 330k. That conflict is AmberSafe's problem, not this checkpoint's, but it will matter when that rung is attested.

LLM360/AmberSafe.notes:
CARD-vs-PAPER CONTRADICTION ON THE BASE, which is why confidence is medium rather than high. CARD (huggingface.co/LLM360/AmberSafe): "We present AmberSafe, a safety-finetuned instruction model using [LLM360/AmberChat](https://huggingface.co/LLM360/AmberChat) as the base." PAPER (arXiv:2312.06550, footnote 6 to section 4.1.3): "The base model for this is checkpoint 355 instead of the last checkpoint" -- i.e. the paper says the starting point is an intermediate Amber pretraining checkpoint (ckpt_355), not the final Amber and not AmberChat. Both are released artifacts, so released_base=yes either way, but the roster's edge (AmberChat -> AmberSafe vs Amber@ckpt_355 -> AmberSafe) is not settled by the sources. RELATED DATASET CONTRADICTION: the card's DataMix lists only PKU-SafeRLHF (330k); the paper says "AmberSafe is trained on ShareGPT 90K" and then "further optimized on the SafeRLHF dataset" -- i.e. the paper describes an SFT-on-ShareGPT stage plus a DPO stage, which would fold AmberChat-like SFT into AmberSafe itself. The card's "Method" section reproduces the DPO repo's two-step recipe ("1. Run supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on the dataset(s) of interest." / "2. Run preference learning on the model from step 1, using preference data") without saying which step the LLM360 team actually re-ran, so it does not resolve the ambiguity. I score method=dpo because that is the operation both sources name for AmberSafe specifically, but if the paper's account is right the checkpoint is closer to an sft+dpo bundle. NOTE ON EXACT QUOTE: the paper writes "Direct Parameter Optimization (DPO)" -- that is the paper's own error for Direct Preference Optimization, quoted as printed. LICENCE MISMATCH WORTH FLAGGING: the checkpoint is released apache-2.0 while its sole training dataset is listed on the same card as cc-by-nc-4.0. DPO hyperparameters from the paper: "We set beta to 0.1, gradient accumulation steps to 4, and the learning rate to 5e-7." ID redirects to IFM/AmberSafe.

METHOD LEFT UNKNOWN ON PURPOSE. The card carries 'C-RLFT' only as a model TAG and in the linked paper title — I fetched both the rendered card and the raw README and neither yielded a prose sentence stating what operation produced this checkpoint. Under the naming-is-not-evidence rule a tag does not establish a method, so method is 'unknown' rather than a guessed sft/rlhf. The algorithm claim IS booked, but its quote comes from the paper (arXiv:2309.11235), not the card, and carries a caveat: the paper's abstract describes C-RLFT in general and its worked example is "openchat-13b fine-tuned with C-RLFT", a LLaMA-based 13B model — NOT this Mistral-based 7B checkpoint. So the algorithm attribution to this specific id is an inference from the shared tag and paper link, not a direct statement about openchat-3.5-0106. If the roster needs method for this row, it should be treated as a documented gap. datasets: not stated in any form I could quote (the paper abstract refers only to "general SFT training data, consisting of a small amount of expert data mixed with a large proportion of sub-optimal data", which names no dataset). The card offers a "Mathematical Reasoning mode", but that is an inference-time prompt template, not evidence of chain-of-thought training, so reasoning stays unknown. Confidence low per the stub rule: the card is silent on training.

[attest-direction-2026-08-16] Ordinary instruct post-training: the card tags C-RLFT and the cited paper (arXiv:2309.11235) describes a single-stage, RL-free conditioned-SFT on mixed-quality ShareGPT-style conversations to "align these models with human goals" — no preference data and no anti-refusal objective. The repo ships no training YAML (weights, tokenizer and openchat.json only), and the shipped data pipeline (ochat/data/generate_dataset.py) reads a plain sharegpt_gpt4.jsonl; no unalignment/toxic-dpo/norefusals dataset appears anywhere. The quoted Safety block is the absence-and-aspiration pattern (residual harmfulness flagged as a limitation to be mitigated downstream), which is standard, not inversion.

[attest-post-training-rungs-2026-08-16] TREE OPENED. /tree/main holds no configs/ directory and no recipe YAML: only .gitattributes, README.md, added_tokens.json, config.json, generation_config.json, 3 safetensors shards + index, openchat.json, and the tokenizer files. `openchat.json` IS the training config and I read it in full — it carries hyperparameters and a base path but NO data pointer: {"local_rank": 0, "model_path": "imone/Mistral_7B_with_EOT_token", "data_prefix": "", "save_path": "", "save_every": 1, "batch_max_len": 77824, "epochs": 5, "lr": 1.1179251066632773e-05, "lr_min_ratio": 0.1, "lr_warmup_ratio": 0.05, "weight_decay": 0.1, "beta1": 0.9, "beta2": 0.95, "eps": 1e-05, "deepspeed": true, "model_type": "openchat_v3.2_mistral", "epoch": 2}. `data_prefix` is empty, so the mix is not recoverable from the repo. config.json confirms _name_or_path "imone/Mistral_7B_with_EOT_token" (Mistral-7B-v0.1 plus an <|end_of_turn|> token, vocab 32002) — this rung is a single fine-tune straight off base.

WHY datasets IS EMPTY AND safety_data IS "unknown". The 0106 card states no mix at all. Its YAML frontmatter is only license/base_model/tags/library_name/pipeline_tag — no `datasets:` key (confirmed in cardData via the HF API), and the card has no "Dataset Details" section; its table of contents runs Usage, Benchmarks, Limitations, License, Citation, Acknowledgements. Per the rule ("unknown means no mix is stated"), that is unknown, not absent. This gap is corroborated on the repo itself: discussion #9 "Instruct-finetuning dataset" (2024-03-31) asks "Hi! What instruct-finetuning dataset was used to train the model?" and the only reply (markding, 2024-05-16) says "I have the same question. The preprint says ShareGPT data 'collected from sharegpt.com' and the code refers to `sharegpt_gpt4.jsonl`. But it would be good if this were more clearly documented on the model card and in a code repository." No maintainer answered.

SECONDARY EVIDENCE, NOT ATTRIBUTED TO THIS CHECKPOINT. The two sibling checkpoints of the same series DO publish a mix, and it contains no safety dataset. openchat/openchat-3.5-1210 (https://huggingface.co/openchat/openchat-3.5-1210/raw/main/README.md): "OpenChat 3.5 was trained with C-RLFT on a collection of publicly available high-quality instruction data, with a custom processing pipeline. We detail some notable subsets included here:" then OpenChat ShareGPT, Open-Orca with FLAN answers (imone/OpenOrca_FLAN), Feedback-Collection (kaist-ai), Capybara (de-contaminated against MT-bench), GOAT, Glaive (glaive-code-assistant), MetaMathQA, MathInstruct, OpenAssistant oasst_top1_2023-08-25 — no shares given for any subset. openchat/openchat_3.5 lists the same minus Feedback-Collection, plus the three Capybara components, and both carry `datasets: openchat/openchat_sharegpt4_dataset` in frontmatter. Chat/instruct/code/math only; no harmlessness, red-team or preference-safety set in either. I did NOT fold these into the datasets field because they are stated for 1210 and 3.5, not for 0106, and the whole point of this pass is not to attribute what a page does not say.

STAGE SHAPE (matters for the within-lineage design). There is no preference rung here. OpenChat's single post-training stage is C-RLFT, which the method paper defines as learning from mixed-quality SFT data WITHOUT preference labels: the abstract (arXiv:2309.11235, read via ar5iv) says the method uses "general SFT training data, consisting of a small amount of expert data mixed with a large proportion of sub-optimal data, without any preference labels", and the data it used there was ShareGPT: "The ShareGPT dataset consists of approximately 70k user-shared conversations, including around 6k expert conversations generated by GPT-4 and the remaining sub-optimal conversations from GPT-3.5." Those counts are the paper's own openchat-3.2/Llama-2 experiments, NOT a stated 0106 mix, so they are not booked as this checkpoint's datasets or size. So 0106 is base -> one conditioned-SFT step; it cannot supply an AmberChat/AmberSafe-style SFT-then-safety-DPO contrast within itself.

INTENT. Quality/benchmark framing throughout, safety explicitly disclaimed rather than targeted. Alongside the quoted headline the same block reads "🚀15-point improvement in Coding over OpenChat-3.5🚀" and "💡 2 Modes: Coding + Generalist, Mathematical Reasoning 💡", and the Limitations section says verbatim: "**Safety** OpenChat may sometimes generate harmful, hate speech, biased responses, or answer unsafe questions. It's crucial to apply additional AI safety measures in use cases that require safe and moderated responses." I classed this helpfulness rather than mixed because the coding/math emphasis reads as benchmark capability within a general quality push; a reader who treats the "Mathematical Reasoning" mode and the coding headline as a stated objective in their own right could defensibly call it mixed (helpfulness + reasoning). Nothing here is uncensoring: no refusal-removal or de-alignment claim appears on any page I opened, and the safety caveat is a disclaimer about an untargeted axis, not a boast.

DEAD ENDS. GitHub imoneoi/openchat README names no dataset for any 3.5 release (its training section only documents the JSON Lines Conversation format); repo root has no configs/ dir (only .github, assets, docker, ochat, pyproject.toml, pytest.ini, SECURITY.md); ochat/data/ contains only generate_dataset.py, whose docstring references a user-supplied `sharegpt_gpt4.jsonl` as an example filename, not a shipped mix; GitHub releases 3.5.0–3.5.2 have empty bodies. The openchat_sharegpt4_dataset card says only "This repository contains cleaned and filtered ShareGPT GPT-4 data used to train OpenChat" — "OpenChat" generically, no checkpoint named, no count. No post-training token or example total is stated anywhere I looked.

TWO ARITHMETIC TRAPS in the shares I recorded, both left exactly as stated rather than reconciled. (1) The SmolTalk2 SFT table totals 19,292.4M tokens while the blog says the SFT mixture "contains 1.8B tokens" - the table is pre-weighting, and the Weight column does the reduction (OpenThoughts3-1.2M_think carries 86.74% of raw tokens at weight 0.02). Cite the weight alongside the share or the mixture reads as 87% reasoning traces. (2) Preference shares are "% of tokens (Chosen)", not total tokens; rejected-side tokens are not tabulated. Every share above is transcribed verbatim from the published tables; none is estimated.

HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B-checkpoints.notes:
NOT A SINGLE CHECKPOINT — it is a revision container, and a roster row treating it as one model will mean whatever revision string it happened to load. Verified against the HF refs API (https://huggingface.co/api/models/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B-checkpoints/refs): 133 branches, of which 118 are stage1/stage2/stage3-step-* pretraining intermediates, 10 are lc-4k-to-32k-step-* / lc-32k-to-64k-step-* long-context stages, and 4 are the post-training revisions it-mid-training, it-SFT, it-soup-APO, it-LC-expert, plus main. Hence two method claims: `revision=` here selects anything from a 94B-token pretraining intermediate to the APO soup. The card's own stage counts — "Stage 1: Steps 0 to 3,450,000 (86 checkpoints)", "Stage 2: Steps 3,450,000 to 4,200,000 (19 checkpoints)", "Stage 3: Steps 4,200,000 to 4,720,000 (13 checkpoints)" — sum to 118 and match the branch listing exactly. Confidence medium not high because the card itself names no dataset and says nothing about reasoning or alignment direction; the substantive documentation lives in the blog and the huggingface/smollm GitHub repo, which describe the RUN, not this repo's revisions.

[attest-direction-2026-08-16] The checkpoints repo itself is mostly pretraining revisions but explicitly ships "checkpoints at every step of our post-training recipe: Mid training, SFT, APO soup, and LC expert", so the SFT operation the roster records is the standard SmolLM3 recipe documented on the SmolLM3-3B card and the SmolLM3 blog. Nothing in the recipe is inverted: SFT uses SmolTalk2 (instruction/reasoning mixtures incl. Tulu 3 SFT Personas IF, OpenHermes-2.5, OpenThoughts3), and the preference stage uses the Tulu 3 8B preference mixture plus synthetic pairs where, per the blog, "generations from Qwen3-32B as 'chosen' and responses from Qwen3-0.6B as 'rejected'" — a capability gap, not refusals as the rejected class. No uncensoring or alignment-removal language, and no toxic/norefusal datasets, appear in any config, dataset card, or the blog. Neither the card nor the blog foregrounds safety data, but absence of emphasis is not inversion.

[attest-post-training-rungs-2026-08-16] WHAT THIS REPO IS. Not a single checkpoint: 167 git branches. 118 are pretraining (stage1/2/3) + 10 long-context, and exactly FOUR are post-training rungs — `it-mid-training`, `it-SFT`, `it-soup-APO`, `it-LC-expert` — which the card names: "We release checkpoints at every step of our post-training recipe: Mid training, SFT, APO soup, and LC expert." Lineage: HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B-Base -> it-mid-training -> it-SFT -> it-soup-APO (-> merged release SmolLM3-3B). The attestation below covers all four rungs.

THE FILE LIST MATTERED, AND SO DID THE NEXT HOP. The repo's own /tree/main holds only .gitattributes and README.md, and the it-SFT branch README is HuggingFace's autogenerated "[More Information Needed]" template — zero evidence there. The recipe configs live one hop out: card -> github.com/huggingface/smollm -> text/finetuning/README.md -> github.com/huggingface/alignment-handbook/tree/main/recipes/smollm3, which holds sft/mid.yaml, sft/sft.yaml, dpo/apo.yaml. I read all three byte-exact (GitHub API, base64-decoded, not a summarizer). Every dataset above is a `dataset_mixture:` entry in one of those three files, with the `weight:` I quote.

STAGE FIELD, since this pass turns on it. Mid-training is marked `other`, not `sft`: it is its own rung (branch `it-mid-training`) with its own config, even though it is executed by scripts/sft.py. Marking it `sft` would collapse two distinct rungs. The preference rung is APO, not vanilla DPO — apo.yaml sets `loss_type: apo_zero`, `beta: 0.05`, 1 epoch; the blog calls it "a variant of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) that provides a more stable optimization objective". The directory is named `dpo/` and the handbook README calls the stage "DPO"; the loss is APO. Do not book this as a DPO rung without that rider.

SAFETY: `absent`, and this is the strong form of absent — a fully stated mix with no safety in it, not a silent card. All 29 post-training datasets are splits of ONE dataset (HuggingFaceTB/smoltalk2) with per-split weights AND published percentage tables. Byte-exact greps: the smoltalk2 card has ZERO occurrences of safe/harmless/refus/toxic/red-team/jailbreak/wildguard/coconot; the blog post likewise returns zero hits for safety/harmless/refusal/toxic/red-team. The only stated data processing is "decontaminate to remove samples present in the benchmarks used for evaluation and remove samples containing emojis". I checked the one transitive path where safety could enter unnamed — allenai/llama-3.1-tulu-3-8b-preference-mixture, the APO non-reasoning half — and its card lists seven constituents (tulu-3-sft-reused-off-policy, tulu-3-sft-reused-on-policy-8b, tulu-3-wildchat-if-on-policy-8b, tulu-3-IF-augmented-on-policy-8b, tulu-3-sft-personas-instruction-following, tulu-3-wildchat-reused-on-policy-8b, tulu-3-ultrafeedback-cleaned-on-policy-8b), none safety. Note this is the 8B preference mixture, which unlike some other Tulu 3 mixtures carries no WildGuardMix/WildJailbreak/CoCoNot subset.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE WITHIN-LINEAGE CONTRAST YOU ARE BUILDING. This lineage does NOT have the AmberChat/AmberSafe shape. No rung introduces safety data, so there is no step here where safety is the only thing that changes — the SmolLM3 rungs are usable as a within-lineage NULL arm (three consecutive post-training steps, one lab, one base, zero safety data at any of them), not as a safety-contrast arm. That is a positive fact about the mix, established from a stated mix, not an unknown.

INTENT = mixed, both components evidenced verbatim on the blog. Reasoning: "we wanted to train the model to reason without targeting a particular domain, such as mathematics or computer code" (mid-training). Helpfulness/instruction-following: the quoted SFT sentence names "instruction following, multilinguality, and tool calling". The APO rung's stated aim is neither safety nor uncensoring: "we performed a round of model alignment using a combination of the Tulu3 preference dataset for non-reasoning mode and new synthetic preference pairs for reasoning mode" — chosen = Qwen3-32B, rejected = Qwen3-0.6B, i.e. a capability-gap preference signal (the same delta-learning shape as OLMo 3's DPO), aimed at "mathematics, science, instruction following, coding, chat, and multilingual tasks". Per rule 3 I did not read "alignment" as safety anywhere.

ONE COUNT DISCREPANCY, flagged not resolved: the blog says the SFT mix comprises "12 non-reasoning datasets and 10 datasets with reasoning traces" (=22); sft.yaml lists 25 entries and the smoltalk2 card says "The total mix consists of 25 datasets" with "10 `think`" and "15 `no_think`". The card and the config agree at 25/15/10; the blog's "12" is the outlier. I report the config's 25.

FINAL RELEASE IS A MERGE, which bears on treating it-soup-APO as the lineage endpoint: "Take each APO checkpoint and create a model 'soup'. Combine the model soup with a mid-training checkpoint that has strong long-content performance. A linear merge with weights of 0.9 and 0.1 for the APO model soup and mid-training checkpoint, respectively, achieved the best performance." So SmolLM3-3B is 0.9*(APO soup) + 0.1*(mid-training), done with MergeKit — the released endpoint is not reachable by any single training step from it-SFT.
