allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Think-SFT.notes:
reasoning = yes is sourced from the card's documented chat template, which emits an explicit <think>...</think> block -- NOT from the model's name (rule 3). This is the one field where Think and Instruct cards genuinely differ: all three Think cards document a <think> chat format, none of the three Instruct cards contain the string '<think>' at all. That is checkpoint-discriminating evidence rather than shared boilerplate. Branch entry point: base_model is the pretrained root, so the Think branch forks from the base in parallel with the Instruct branch rather than descending from it. Note the Safety eval row on the Think cards has an EMPTY benchmark-name cell ('| **Safety** |  | 65.8 | ...'), unlike the Instruct cards, and Think safety scores are markedly lower (65.8 vs 89.2 for the SFT stage); I have still recorded direction = standard because nothing on the card describes removing refusals or de-censoring, but a roster treating Think and Instruct as interchangeable on safety posture would be wrong.

[attest-post-training-rungs-2026-08-16] STAGE: this is the SFT rung of the Olmo 3 7B Think lineage (base allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B → Think-SFT → Think-DPO → Think RLVR). Nothing here is DPO; the DPO rung has its own mix (Dolci-Think-DPO-7B), not read in this pass.

WHY 'mixed': three intents are each separately evidenced on the Dolci-Think-SFT-7B card. (1) REASONING is the stated organising principle — "Sources include a mixture of existing reasoning traces:" and "New prompts and new reasoning traces from us"; every datapoint carries "<think>...</think>". (2) HELPFULNESS/instruction-following — the model card says the SFT set "consits of math, code, chat, and general knowledge queries" and the mix includes Dolci Precise IF, Persona IF, WildChat, Aya, TableGPT. (3) SAFETY is present as named data, not inferred: CoCoNot (10,227), WildGuardMix (38,315), WildJailbreak (41,100) — the same three safety sources the CLAUDE.md notes for Olmo 3 generally. The model card also reports a "Safety" evaluation row (65.8 for this checkpoint).

SHARES: every component count above is quoted as printed on the dataset card ("prompts", except Olmo Identity "samples"). I did NOT compute any percentage; note that the component counts are in PROMPTS while the split total (2,268,178) is in EXAMPLES, so the two are not straightforwardly commensurable and any safety-share fraction would be a derived number, not a stated one.

CAVEAT ON REPO IDENTITY: the Dolci-Think-SFT-7B card ends with "This dataset was used for 7B post-training, the [7B dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/Dolci-Think-SFT) is slightly different." That sentence is self-contradictory on a repo already named -7B (likely a copy-paste from the 32B card); allenai/Dolci-Think-SFT is a separate live repo. The model card's own metadata tags allenai/Dolci-Think-SFT-7B as the dataset, and its prose links "Dolci-Think-SFT-7B" to the URL /datasets/allenai/dolci-thinking-sft — a third identifier. I attest against the tagged repo Dolci-Think-SFT-7B; if the campaign needs the exact mix bytes, the three repos should be diffed.

FILE-LIST RESULT (the point of this pass): negative — the model repo carries no training config, recipe YAML, or trainer_state.json, only weights/tokenizer/README plus a small fix_tokens.py. All composition evidence here comes from the dataset card, not from a hidden config.

NOT-ASSERTED: no per-stage safety percentage for this checkpoint is stated anywhere I opened. The CLAUDE.md figure "~5% of SFT (110k of 2.15M prompts)" comes from the Olmo 3 report (arXiv:2512.13961), which I did not open in this pass and which describes the Instruct/overall pipeline; do not silently transfer it onto this Think-SFT mix.

allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Think-DPO.notes:
Cleanest card in the branch: YAML base_model, YAML datasets and the release-table row all agree that this is the Think-branch DPO stage trained on Dolci-Think-DPO-7B from Think-SFT. Unlike Instruct-DPO, the declared dataset is branch-consistent here. No named optimiser distinct from the operation, so no algorithm claim. No post-training token or example count on the card.

[attest-post-training-rungs-2026-08-16] TREE/MAIN CHECKED: the repo file list holds NO training YAML, recipe config, or trainer_state.json — only weights, tokenizer, config.json, generation_config.json, chat_template.jinja, olmo-think.png, README.md. So the recipe evidence had to come from the named dataset, and it did.

WHY "mixed", and where each leg is evidenced. (a) reasoning/helpfulness: the DPO stage line quoted above, plus the card's opening "Long chain-of-thought thinking improves reasoning tasks like math and coding" (same URL) — the stated content of the DPO mix is math, code, chat, general knowledge. (b) safety: the card NEVER states a safety goal, but the mixture it names demonstrably contains explicit safety/red-team data. The card's own prose is in fact anti-safety-claiming: "Like any base language model or fine-tuned model without safety filtering, these models can easily be prompted by users to generate harmful and sensitive content."

THE SAFETY EVIDENCE IS IN THE MIXTURE, NOT THE PROSE. The Dolci-Think-DPO-7B card gives no source breakdown at all ("It contains 150,000 preference pairs created with the preference heuristic described in Delta Learning (Geng et al. 2025)."), so I pulled the dataset_source column frequencies from the HF datasets-server statistics endpoint. Verbatim from https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/statistics?dataset=allenai%2FDolci-Think-DPO-7B&config=default&split=train :
  "tulu_v3.9_wildjailbreak_decontaminated_50k":3885
  "tulu_v3.9_synthetic_finalresp_wildguardmixtrain_decontaminated_50k":3884
  "tulu-3-sft-coconot-regenerated":790
Three named safety/non-compliance corpora, 8,559 rows of the 150,000 stated total. Every share above is a COUNT taken from that endpoint; none is estimated, and the endpoint reports "partial":false so the counts cover the whole split.

THE STAGE MATTERS AND SO DOES THE PREFERENCE HEURISTIC — this is the field that decides whether this rung is a within-lineage safety contrast, and here it is NOT. From the same statistics call, every one of the 150,000 pairs has "preference_type":{"delta_learning":150000}, "chosen_model":{"qwen3-reasoning-32b":150000}, "rejected_model":{"qwen3-reasoning-0.6b":150000}. The preference signal is a CAPABILITY GAP between a 32B and a 0.6B reasoning model applied uniformly across all 24 sources — it is not a harmlessness annotation. So even on the ~5.7% of rows sourced from wildjailbreak/wildguardmix/coconot, what the DPO objective rewards is the bigger model's answer, not a human safety judgement. This checkpoint is NOT an AmberSafe-shaped rung (DPO on a safety set alone); its safety content is a minority of prompts inside a helpfulness/reasoning preference objective.

ONE CARD INCONSISTENCY, FLAGGED NOT RESOLVED: the Stage 2 line lists both Dolci-Think-DPO-7B and Dolci-Instruct-DPO-7B, but the YAML frontmatter lists only "allenai/Dolci-Think-DPO-7B", and the Instruct-DPO card says it "was used to preference tune Olmo 3 Instruct 7B". The Stage-1 and Stage-3 lines pair a Think and an Instruct dataset the same way, so this reads as a template listing both variants' datasets per stage rather than a claim that both fed this checkpoint. I list it but mark its contribution here unstated. The Instruct-DPO dataset does not resolve under the name Dolci-Instruct-DPO-7B on the datasets-server (null return), so I did not get counts for it.

The card's evaluation table does carry a "Safety" benchmark row (SFT 65.8 → DPO 67.7 → RLVR 70.7), which is a measured outcome, not a stated objective, and I did not treat it as intent evidence on its own.

allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Think.notes:
Terminal checkpoint of the Think branch; YAML, release table and dataset declaration are mutually consistent. Same algorithm gap as the Instruct final: the card names the operation ('reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards') but no optimiser, and no card in this lineage mentions GRPO or PPO. The Olmo 3 paper did not close it either at the level of a quotable sentence, so algorithm = unknown rather than a guess. Reasoning is evidenced by the documented <think> chat template, not by the name.

[attest-post-training-extra-2026-08-16] TREE CHECKED, NOTHING THERE: /tree/main holds only .gitattributes, .tokenizer_config.json.swp, README.md, chat_template.jinja, config.json, generation_config.json, merges.txt, three model-*.safetensors shards + index, olmo-think.png, special_tokens_map.json, tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json, vocab.json. No configs/ directory, no training YAML, no trainer_state.json. All composition evidence therefore comes from the three Dolci dataset cards the README names.

THREE POST-TRAINING STAGES, all named on the model card verbatim: "supervised fine-tuning on the Dolci-Think-SFT-7B dataset. This dataset consits of math, code, chat, and general knowledge queries." / "direct preference optimization on the Dolci-Think-DPO-7B dataset." / "reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards on the Dolci-Think-RL-7B dataset. This dataset consits of math, code, instruction-following, and general chat queries." (sic, "consits", verbatim from https://huggingface.co/allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Think/raw/main/README.md).

WHY mixed, both legs evidenced. (a) reasoning — the model card's stated aim, quoted above; the SFT card also states the mixture "combines existing reasoning traces with new prompts and traces". (b) safety — the SFT mixture card itemises three explicit safety/red-team sets with counts: WildJailbreak 41,100, WildGuardMix 38,315, CoCoNot 10,227, i.e. 89,642 of the stated Total: 2,268,178 (~4.0%; that ratio is arithmetic on two stated counts, not an estimate of an unstated share). Safety is not stated as a GOAL anywhere on the model card — the stages are described only as math/code/chat/general-knowledge — so the safety leg rests on named data, not on stated intent. If your gate wants intent-as-stated only, this checkpoint reads `reasoning`; safety_data would still be `present`.

STAGE ASSIGNMENT OF THE SAFETY DATA (this is the field that matters for a within-lineage contrast). Safety data is unambiguously in the SFT stage, with counts. At the DPO stage the card gives NO source breakdown at all — only "150,000 preference pairs" built with the Delta Learning heuristic (Geng et al. 2025). The safety-adjacent DPO source I list, tulu_v3.9_wildjailbreak_decontaminated_50k, was read off the dataset VIEWER's `dataset` column on https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/Dolci-Think-DPO-7B, not off any prose in the card; treat it as weaker evidence than the SFT table, and its share is genuinely unknown (the card gives no per-source counts). At the RLVR stage the itemised mix is math/code/IF/general with no safety set named — that stage reads `absent` on its own, though I have coded the checkpoint-level field `present` because the SFT stage dominates the answer.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE AmberChat/AmberSafe-STYLE CONTRAST: this lineage does NOT have that shape. Olmo 3 Think does not isolate safety at a single rung — safety data is folded into the SFT mixture alongside reasoning and IF data, so no step in base → SFT → DPO → RLVR changes safety data and nothing else. Useful as a negative case for the within-lineage design, not as an instance of it.

DERIVED, NOT MEASURED: the ~4.0% figure above and the per-stage split are arithmetic on stated counts; no proportion in the `datasets` array is estimated — every share is a count or "unknown" exactly as the card gives it.

allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125.notes:
THE INDEPENDENCE FINDING. The card calls this model "an improved version of OLMoE-09-24" and says main was "annealed from `step1200000-tokens5033B`" — but that branch does not exist in THIS repo. Repo-structure evidence (HF refs API): allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125 has 16 branches, ALL of the form stage2-ingredient{1,2,3}-step*-tokens* topping out at 101B tokens; there is no stage-1 branch. allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 has 246 branches carrying the full stage-1 trajectory including step1200000-tokens5033B, plus only main and fp32 beyond it. Conclusion: 0125 = the 0924 stage-1 pretraining trunk + a NEW ~101B-token stage-2 anneal on dolmino-mix-1124 (three candidate 'ingredients' were released; the 0924 anneal was the same 23,842 steps on a different mix). Both cards carry word-for-word identical branch text, which is why this is easy to miss. released_base is 'yes' not 'na' precisely because the checkpoint it was annealed from IS publicly released — as a branch of the 0924 repo.

UNRESOLVED: the card defers to "the [paper appendix](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.02060) for details", but I could not find any mention of 0125, January 2025, or dolmino in arXiv:2409.02060 (abstract page and v2 PDF both checked; PDF text extraction was partial, so this is a failure to confirm, not a confirmed absence).

CONTRADICTION (card vs its own siblings): this base card's link block describes the adaptation recipe as "**SFT** ... [Data](https://hf.co/datasets/allenai/tulu-v3.1-mix-preview-4096-OLMoE)" and "**DPO/KTO (Direct Preference Optimization/Kahneman-Tversky Optimization)**, [Checkpoints](https://huggingface.co/allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct), [Preference Data](https://hf.co/datasets/allenai/ultrafeedback_binarized_cleaned)". The four stage cards instead name tulu-3-sft-olmo-2-mixture, olmoe-0125-1b-7b-preference-mix and RLVR-GSM, treat DPO and Instruct as separate checkpoints, and never mention KTO. The base card's block is 0924-era text carried over (it also links the 0924 wandb logs); the stage cards are the better source for the 0125 recipe.

reasoning: no card text addresses chain-of-thought training, so 'unknown' rather than 'no'. direction is 'na': pretraining/annealing stage, no refusal training defined.

allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-SFT.notes:

Avoid harmful, unethical, prejudiced, or negative content.") under which the model "properly declines to answer 100% of the harmful questions" from 175 unsafe prompts, plus a self-reflection classifier prompt (precision 99.4%, recall 95.6%) (https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06825v1). HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B-checkpoints@it-.notes:
[attest-post-training-rungs-2026-08-16] WHAT THIS CHECKPOINT IS. The repo's own README says "We release checkpoints at every step of our post-training recipe: Mid training, SFT, APO soup, and LC expert." The branch list confirms the ladder: it-mid-training -> it-SFT -> it-soup-APO -> it-LC-expert. `it-soup-APO` is the preference-stage output: apo.yaml starts from `model_name_or_path: HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B-checkpoints` / `model_revision: it-SFT` and trains with `loss_type: apo_zero`, `beta: 0.05`, `num_train_epochs: 1`. "soup" is a weight average, not a data stage — blog step 1: "Take each APO checkpoint and create a model 'soup'." (Step 2, the 0.9/0.1 linear merge with a long-context mid-training checkpoint, is the SEPARATE `it-LC-expert` branch, so it is not folded into this one.)

WHERE THE EVIDENCE IS. The branch's own /tree/main holds only weights + tokenizer + a stub README (auto-generated transformers template, every field "[More Information Needed]"); the main-branch README holds no mixture either. The actual composition is in the alignment-handbook recipes the smollm repo's finetuning README points to — apo.yaml, sft.yaml, mid.yaml — which name every split by id/config/split with explicit `weight:` fields. Those YAMLs are the source for every share above.

SAFETY: ABSENT, AND THE MIX IS FULLY ENUMERATED. The APO mix is exactly two splits; the SFT mix is exactly 25 splits; the mid mix is exactly two. Not one is a safety, harmlessness, red-team, refusal or jailbreak set (no coconot, wildguardmix, wildjailbreak, PKU-SafeRLHF, hh-rlhf, etc.). The blog contains zero occurrences of safety/harmless/red-team/toxic/refusal/jailbreak/guard. The SmolLM3-3B card's only safety-adjacent text is a generic disclaimer about factuality and bias, not a training claim. So this is `absent` in the strong sense: a stated mix was read and safety was not in it.

ONE RESIDUAL CAVEAT ON `absent`, DECLARED. The `no_think` half of the APO data is allenai/llama-3.1-tulu-3-8b-preference-mixture, whose card lists 7 component datasets, none safety-named; but one of them, allenai/tulu-3-sft-reused-off-policy, says only that it "contains prompts from our SFT mixture" and gives no prompt-source breakdown. The Tulu 3 SFT mixture is known to contain a safety component, so a small unquantified safety fraction could ride in two levels down. Nothing in any SmolLM3 source states this, and no share is recoverable, so I did not list it as a dataset. Treat `absent` as "absent at every level the sources enumerate."

INTENT = mixed, both arms quoted. Helpfulness/quality: the APO data is a general preference mixture and the stated payoff is benchmark performance — "While downstream evaluations showed improvements across mathematics, science, instruction following, coding, chat, and multilingual tasks" and "The APO objective has been shown to be more stable, and we also observed higher downstream performance in our internal ablations" (both on https://huggingface.co/blog/smollm3). Reasoning: the stage explicitly builds thinking-mode preference pairs — "To ensure full coverage of all domains in the non-thinking dataset, we generated complementing thinking mode preference pairs" — and the checkpoint sits downstream of 140B tokens of reasoning mid-training. Neither arm is safety.

FOR THE WITHIN-LINEAGE CONTRAST. This lineage does NOT have the AmberChat/AmberSafe shape. The it-SFT -> it-soup-APO step changes optimizer objective (SFT -> apo_zero) and data (25 instruction splits -> 2 preference splits), with no safety data on either side, so the step isolates preference optimisation for helpfulness+reasoning, not safety. Useful as a NEGATIVE control for a safety-step contrast, and as a clean helpfulness/reasoning-only preference step. Note also the DPO-style delta-learning structure on the think half — Qwen3-32B chosen vs Qwen3-0.6B rejected — which is the same capability-gap construction the campaign already documents for OLMo 3's DPO.

Corroborated independently by the linked MosaicML/Databricks blog, which spells the acronym out — MPT-7B-Chat was "finetuned using ShareGPT-Vicuna, HC3, Alpaca, Helpful and Harmless, and Evol-Instruct datasets" (https://www.databricks.com/blog/mpt-7b).

The safety leg rests ENTIRELY on hh-rlhf's inclusion; MosaicML states no safety or harmlessness objective in prose anywhere I opened. If a downstream analysis requires a *stated* safety objective rather than safety data in the mix, this checkpoint should be scored helpfulness, not mixed. The safety_data field carries the defensible fact; the intent field carries a schema-definitional call. The blog's only safety-adjacent sentence is about the ChatML format helping "prevent malicious prompt injection", which is a serving-format property, not post-training data.

So this lineage supplies a clean SFT -> DPO pair but NO base layer. Any base->SFT or base->superego statistic computed with control-hf standing in for the base is measuring an SFT checkpoint against its own DPO child, not a pretraining->alignment contrast.

google/gemma-2-9b.summary: google/gemma-2-9b (root, Google) → google/gemma-2-9b-it (instruction-tuned). Two checkpoints, both live and readable on HF but gated behind Google's licence acceptance (the rendered pages fetch fine; https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-2-9b/raw/main/README.md returns HTTP 401). THE CRITICAL FINDING IS ABOUT THE ROOT AND IT IS NOT ON THE MODEL CARD. The Gemma 2 technical report (arXiv:2408.00118) states in its abstract that the 9B was trained by knowledge distillation from a teacher rather than by next-token prediction: "We also train the 2B and 9B models with knowledge distillation (Hinton et al., 2015) instead of next token prediction." The HF card for google/gemma-2-9b never mentions distillation at all — it reports only the 8T token count and the corpus categories. Since the task's definition of DERIVED explicitly includes "distilled", I have set root.independent = "no". Read the nuance in root.derived_from and the notes before using this in the statistics: the 9B's weights are NOT initialised from another checkpoint and it is a full 8-trillion-token pretraining run of its own, so it is not derived in the pruned/upscaled/continued-pretraining sense; what is inherited is the training SIGNAL, from a teacher the report never names. Whether that counts as a dependent observation for your roster hinges on whether the (unnamed) teacher or its siblings — notably google/gemma-2-27b, which the report says was trained on 13T tokens by ordinary next-token prediction — also appear in the roster. If the roster contains no other Gemma-2 lineage, treating this as one independent pretraining run is defensible; if it contains gemma-2-27b, it is not. I could not resolve the teacher's identity from the primary source and did not guess. Post-training for the -it checkpoint is documented ONLY in the paper (SFT → RLHF → model merging); the -it card itself says nothing about method, algorithm, datasets, or example counts, so per rule 6 its confidence is "low" despite the paper evidence. My remaining web-search budget was exhausted mid-audit (200/200), so everything here comes from four primary-source WebFetches: the two HF cards, the arXiv abstract page, and the paper's HTML (arxiv.org/html and ar5iv).

microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning-plus.summary:
microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning-plus is a single-checkpoint lineage sitting two post-training steps above a Microsoft-pretrained root. The pretraining run is microsoft/phi-4 (14B dense decoder-only, 9.8T tokens, no base_model in its HF frontmatter, i.e. from scratch). Phi-4-reasoning = SFT of phi-4 on ~1.4M CoT prompt/response pairs whose responses were generated by OpenAI's o3-mini (16B training tokens). Phi-4-reasoning-plus = a further outcome-based RL (GRPO) pass on top of Phi-4-reasoning over ~6,400 verifiable math problems. All three checkpoints (microsoft/phi-4, microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning, microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning-plus) are live public repos on HF (API 200 on all three, checked 2026-08-15), all MIT.

INDEPENDENCE CAVEAT FOR THE STATISTICS, read before counting: the pretraining run underlying this lineage is Microsoft's own and is not shared with any other lab, so as a pretraining observation it is independent. But the named root here is NOT a pretraining checkpoint — it is a post-training derivative of microsoft/phi-4. If the roster elsewhere contains microsoft/phi-4, Phi-4-reasoning, Phi-4-mini, Phi-4-mini-reasoning, or any other phi-4 descendant as a separate lineage, those are the SAME pretraining run counted twice and must be collapsed to one unit. I cannot check the roster from here; flagging it as the live double-counting risk.

SECOND CAVEAT, weaker but real: the SFT stage is distillation from o3-mini, so the reasoning behaviour of this lineage is not independent of OpenAI's o3-mini in the way its pretraining is independent of other labs. Whether that matters depends on what the statistic is over.

NOT derived from any other organisation's checkpoint: Llama 3's architecture and tokenizer were adopted, but the report states "Note that while we use the Llama 3 tokenizer, we do not utilize either the weights or the outputs of Llama 3 during the training of Kanana."
root.tokens: Root from-scratch run (Kanana-8B): 3T tokens = 2.7T (stage 1) + 300B (stage 2). Kanana 1.5 update on top: 100B (stage 1) + up to 10B (stage 2) of additional pretraining, plus a separate long-context extension stage.
root.data: 3T-token bilingual English/Korean corpus categorised as English web, Korean web, academic, code, encyclopedic documents and instruction data, all from publicly available sources, filtered with a DCLM classifier (English) and an iteratively retrained FineWeb-Edu-style fastText edu classifier (Korean); the 1.5 update added synthetically generated high-quality math and code corpora seeded from NuminaMath and permissively licensed open-source code.

kakaocorp/kanana-1.5-8b-base.summary: kakaocorp/kanana-1.5-8b-base is NOT a from-scratch checkpoint in its own right: it is continued pretraining (~110B tokens, 100B stage 1 + up to 10B stage 2, plus a long-context stage that raised RoPE base frequency from 500K to 8M and extended 8K->32K, then YaRN to 128K) on top of Kakao's own Kanana-8B-Base. Kanana-8B-Base WAS trained from scratch by Kakao on 3T tokens (2.7T stage 1 + 300B stage 2) and was never publicly released (the Feb 2025 report released only the 2.1B tier; the HF kakaocorp org listing contains no kanana-8b-base). CRITICAL CONFOUND CHECKED AND CLEARED: the config.json of both checkpoints is architecturally identical to Llama-3-8B (LlamaForCausalLM, 32 layers, hidden 4096, intermediate 14336, 32 heads / 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, vocab 128256, bos 128000) and could easily be misread as a Llama-3 derivative. The technical report states outright that Kakao adopted Llama 3's architecture and tokenizer deliberately as a control, and did not use Llama 3's weights or outputs. So the lineage traces entirely to Kakao's own pretraining run and counts as an INDEPENDENT observation. kakaocorp/kanana-1.5-8b-instruct-2505 is the aligned sibling; the two HF cards are byte-for-byte identical shared boilerplate and neither documents training at all, so every method/data claim below comes from the lab's arXiv report (Kanana 1.0) and its Korean-language dev blog (Kanana 1.5).

m-a-p/neo_7b.summary: "MAP-Neo 7B: an independent pretraining run, not a derivative. m-a-p/neo_7b was trained from scratch on 4.5T tokens of the lab's own bilingual Matrix corpus (fundamental phase ~3.7T + decay phase 720B), so this lineage counts as a genuine independent observation. Chain: neo_7b (pretrain) -> neo_7b_sft_v0.1 (two-phase SFT: >2M instruction points for 3 epochs, then >100k real multi-turn dialogues for 1 epoch) -> neo_7b_instruct_v0.1 (three-iteration Iterative DPO on Nectar prompts labelled by Starling-RM-34B, plus a Chinese preference set in iteration 3). All three released Apache-2.0; all three parents are publicly released, so every edge is traceable. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON EVIDENCE QUALITY: all three HF cards are the same NEO-series template — neo_7b_sft_v0.1 and neo_7b_instruct_v0.1 are byte-identical (3,721 bytes, diff clean), and neo_7b differs only in its usage code block. Per-checkpoint documentation on HF is therefore one row of a shared table; everything else is sourced from arXiv:2405.19327, which the cards cite. No repo carries base_model metadata. The paper's names ('Neo-7B-SFT', 'Neo-7B-Instruct') are never explicitly tied to the '_v0.1' repo suffixes, so the paper->repo mapping is documentary inference from the card rows, not a stated identity. One roster-relevant nuance: the instruct card implies it is tuned from neo_7b, but the paper places it downstream of the SFT checkpoint."

meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B.summary: All 12 checkpoints descend from a single pretraining run, meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B, so this roster contributes ONE independent observation, not 12. Internal structure: (a) Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is Meta's own post-train of the root; (b) the Tulu chain is root -> Tulu-3-8B-SFT -> Tulu-3-8B-DPO -> Tulu-3.1-8B, each stage separately released; (c) the four *-SFT-no-*-data checkpoints are SIBLINGS of Tulu-3-8B-SFT, not descendants of it — they are alternative SFTs off the same root, so they are near-duplicates of each other, differing (by name only, see below) in one ablated data source; (d) Hermes-3, Dolphin-3.0 and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B are three independent third-party post-trains of the root. Note for any statistic treating these as replicates: Tulu-3-8B-DPO and Tulu-3.1-8B share the entire chain up to DPO, and the roster includes Tulu-3.1-8B (GRPO) but NOT allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B (the original PPO RLVR final), so the PPO-vs-GRPO contrast the algorithm field exists to capture is only half-present here. LAB COUNTRY EVIDENCE (no room for it in the lab quote field): the Llama 3.1 LICENSE names the entity and jurisdiction — "“Meta” or “we” means Meta Platforms Ireland Limited (if you are located in or, if you are an entity, your principal place of business is in the EEA or Switzerland) and Meta Platforms, Inc. (if you are located outside of the EEA or Switzerland)." and "This Agreement will be governed and construed under the laws of the State of California without regard to choice of law principles" — hence US/California for the training entity. METHOD NOTE: quotes drawn from arXiv HTML renderings (2407.21783v3, 2408.11857v1) were re-verified by fetching the raw HTML and string-matching, because the fetch summarizer misrendered one Llama 3 sentence on first pass (it returned "supervised finetuning (SFT) on instruction tuning data and Direct Preference Optimization"; the paper actually reads "supervised finetuning (SFT) followed by Direct Preference Optimization"). Every paper quote below is the string-matched raw text, and inline citation markers such as "( Rafailov et al. 2024 , DPO;)" and "[ 9 ]" are artifacts of HTML-to-text conversion, not my insertions.

tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Base.summary: Falcon3 (TII). Root tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Base is pretrained from scratch on 14 Teratokens; every other checkpoint in the roster descends from it by an architectural operation, not just post-training. Falcon3-10B-Base is depth up-scaled from the 7B base plus 2T tokens of continual pretraining; Falcon3-3B-Base is pruned (depth+width) from the 7B base and healed on 100 GT with a knowledge-distillation objective; Falcon3-1B-Base is pruned from the 3B model (healed using the 3B and 7B models) on 80 GT, so it is a grandchild of the root via 3B. The four *-Instruct checkpoints each sit on the matching *-Base and are documented only as a single undifferentiated post-training pass on 1.2 million samples -- no card names SFT, DPO, RLHF or any optimiser, so all four are method instruct_bundle. STATISTICAL CONSEQUENCE: all 8 checkpoints share the single 14T pretraining run of Falcon3-7B-Base. This is ONE independent pretraining observation, not eight and not four -- the 1B/3B/10B bases are derived weights (prune/distill/upscale) from that same run, not separate pretraining runs.

Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B.summary:
Root Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B is an independently pretrained base (18T tokens, Qwen Team / Alibaba Cloud). Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is its post-trained sibling and sits directly on it (frontmatter `base_model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B`).

LINEAGE DISCREPANCY — READ BEFORE COUNTING THIS AS A THREE-CHECKPOINT LINEAGE ON Qwen2.5-7B. deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B is NOT trained from Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B. Both primary sources say its base is Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B: the model card's own download table pairs "DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B" with "[Qwen2.5-Math-7B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B)", and the R1 paper says "The base models we use here are Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B, Qwen2.5-Math-7B, Qwen2.5-14B, Qwen2.5-32B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct." Note that the 14B and 32B distills DO use plain Qwen2.5 bases — only the 1.5B and 7B use the Math variants, so this is a per-size fact, not a blanket one.

Corroborated mechanically from the weights' own configs (not just the cards): DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B/config.json has rope_theta=10000, sliding_window=4096; Qwen2.5-Math-7B has rope_theta=10000, sliding_window=4096, max_position_embeddings=4096; Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B has rope_theta=1000000.0, sliding_window=131072. The distill inherits the Math-7B rope base, not the general-7B one.

Qwen2.5-Math-7B is itself declared as derived from Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B (its HF frontmatter reads `base_model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B`), so the root of the whole lineage is still Qwen2.5-7B — but transitively, through a math-specialised continued-pretraining intermediate that is NOT in the roster. For an independence count the lineage is intact (one pretraining run underneath all three). For any claim that treats the three checkpoints as base / instruct / reasoning-branch of the SAME checkpoint, it is not: the reasoning branch forks at Qwen2.5-Math-7B, a 4K-context math model, and any base-vs-distill logit comparison run against Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B is comparing across an unmodelled intermediate.

From it: SmolLM3-3B-checkpoints is a multi-revision container (133 branches) holding the pretraining intermediates (stage1/2/3 every 40,000 steps), the two long-context extension stages, and the post-training revisions (it-mid-training, it-SFT, it-soup-APO, it-LC-expert); SmolLM3-3B is the single released aligned model, produced by reasoning mid-training (~140B tokens) -> SFT (1.8B-token mixture, 4 epochs) -> APO alignment -> a linear merge of an APO model soup with a mid-training checkpoint. allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B.summary: Single-lab, single-root lineage. `allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B` is a from-scratch pretrain by Ai2 on its own Dolma 3 corpus (5.93T tokens, three staged phases), with NO `base_model` field in its card YAML and no mention anywhere of pruning, upscaling, distillation, or continued pretraining from a third-party checkpoint. From that root the card's release table declares two parallel post-training branches, each base -> SFT -> DPO -> RLVR: the Instruct branch (Instruct-SFT -> Instruct-DPO -> Instruct) and the Think branch (Think-SFT -> Think-DPO -> Think). Every link in both chains is corroborated by the checkpoint's own YAML `base_model` field, so the chain is verifiable checkpoint-by-checkpoint rather than only by the family table. All seven repos are public, ungated, Apache-2.0, and returned HTTP 200. IMPORTANT CAVEAT FOR THE AUDITOR, see per-checkpoint notes: the prose "Model Details / Stage 1: SFT / Stage 2: DPO / Stage 3: RLVR" block is IDENTICAL boilerplate on all six post-trained cards (diff-verified) and describes the whole pipeline, not the checkpoint you are reading. It therefore cannot be used as evidence that a given id is the SFT or the DPO stage, and I did not use it that way. The checkpoint-specific evidence I used is the YAML `base_model`/`datasets` fields and the release-table row in which each id appears.

allenai/Olmo-3-1125-32B.summary:
allenai/Olmo-3-1125-32B (base, pretrained from scratch on Dolma 3) → allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct-SFT (SFT) → allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct-DPO (DPO) → allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct (RLVR, final). The chain is established by the YAML `base_model` field on each card, which links each stage to the previous one, and is corroborated by the release table reproduced identically on all four cards (rows: Base Model / SFT / DPO / Final Models (RLVR); column "Olmo 3.1 32B Instruct"). All four repos resolved HTTP 200 on 2026-08-15; none are gated or withdrawn.

CRITICAL CAVEAT ON THE POST-TRAINING CARDS: the three post-training cards (SFT, DPO, Instruct) are ONE TEMPLATE. `diff` on the raw README.md files shows the prose bodies are byte-identical apart from the model id substituted into the title and code snippets, plus one extra NOTE on the Instruct card. In particular the "## Model Details" section listing "#### Stage 1: SFT", "#### Stage 2:DPO", "#### Stage 3: RLVR" appears in full on ALL THREE cards. That section therefore describes the PIPELINE, not the checkpoint whose card you are reading — the SFT card's own body claims a DPO and an RLVR stage. Checkpoint-specific evidence comes only from (a) the YAML `base_model` and `datasets` fields, which DO differ per card, and (b) the release table row containing that exact model id. My method claims rest on the table row and the base_model chain; where I quote the templated stage prose I say so.

CONTRADICTION (card-internal, all three post-training cards): the templated stage prose names 7B THINK datasets — "supervised fine-tuning on the Dolci-Think-SFT-7B dataset", "Datasets: Dolci-Think-SFT-7B, Dolci-Instruct-SFT" — on cards for 32B INSTRUCT models. The YAML frontmatter of each card names only the Instruct-line dataset (Dolci-Instruct-SFT / Dolci-Instruct-DPO / Dolci-Instruct-RL). The "-7B" suffix on a 32B card and the "Think" name on an Instruct card both indicate copy-paste from the 7B Think card. I report the datasets field with BOTH sets named and flag which source gives which. Typos preserved throughout: the cards read "consits" and "Stage 2:DPO" (no space).

LAB COUNTRY IS NOT SOURCED. No page I fetched (model cards, https://huggingface.co/allenai, https://allenai.org/) states a city or country. I report country "United States" as background knowledge, NOT as a sourced claim — no quote backs it, and it should be treated as unverified in this audit. org_type IS sourced: the HF organisation page carries a literal "non-profit" badge (verbatim string "non-profit" in the page HTML).

PAPER MATERIAL, REPORTED SECOND-HAND AND NOT FILED AS CLAIMS: fetches of https://arxiv.org/html/2512.13961v1 returned two strings I could not independently re-verify character-for-character, so I have filed no claim on them: "We first train Olmo 3 Base on Dolma 3 Mix, our 6T token pretraining data mix." and "We introduce Olmo 3.1 Think 32B to illustrate that extended OlmoRL training leads to improved performance." Two consequences. (1) The paper's "6T token pretraining data mix" describes the MIX SIZE; the card states 5.50 Trillion training tokens for the 32B. These are different quantities (corpus size vs tokens consumed) and not necessarily a contradiction, but a roster recording "6T" for this model would be recording the wrong number. (2) The paper names its RL system "OlmoRL" but the retrieved text contained no occurrence of "GRPO", "PPO", or "policy optimization"; and the OlmoRL sentence concerns Olmo 3.1 Think 32B, a DIFFERENT model from the Instruct line audited here. I therefore file `algorithm` as unknown on every checkpoint. This is exactly the Tulu-3 vs Tulu-3.1 case the schema warns about: the operation (RLVR) is sourced, the optimiser is not, and a roster that fills in "GRPO" here would be guessing.
